title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
authors: Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, Omar Khattab
summary: GPT-6 Astra names what networks were trained on from their weights alone, repairs a stuck Kinetix car policy (0% to 100%, 3.5% of weights, one reply, no tools), writes MinAtar and 9x9 Go networks from zero, and lifts Qwen3.5-0.8B on MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% by removing a loop direction (0.016% of weights). Edits removed a blocker; they did not add a missing ability (Gemma 3 270M: no gain).

title: Astra weight edits on a VLA, a world action model and humanoid control
summary: π0.5 on 5 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks: 27% to 65% with about 4 edits on held-out episodes; on one task 4 of 3.6B parameters took success from 28/92 to 82/92. FastWAM gains 8.7 points. Unitree G1 policies adapt to a hidden payload by rewiring waist and knee gains. Candidates are found by probing saved inputs offline, then checked with rollouts. Each edited π0.5 was fine-tuned on one task, so gains hold for that task only; no code or paper as of 2026-11-05.

title: Weight-Space Programming for VLAs
summary: Changing one number in SmolVLA (the x-action output bias) lifts a LIBERO-Spatial task from 42/100 to 64/100 on unseen initial states (Fisher p = 0.003). The fault was read off rollouts: the gripper closed too far along x and regrasped.

title: Policy Surgery
summary: GPT-OSS-120B edits a 4,996-parameter LunarLander PPO actor after its dynamics change. Reversed thrusters: 0 to 226 of 256 held-out episodes. Crosswind and reduced thrust gain 3 to 6 points, and only one of those intervals excludes zero. Separate selection, approval and test seeds, with every failure kept.

title: Weight-space programming autoresearch
summary: Claude, running as a coding agent, hand-writes transformer weights: 959 programs, and all 10 algorithmic tasks reach 100% within three attempts. A second test is mostly negative: Claude Opus 5.5 reading Qwen3.5-0.8B weights predicts the effects of 420 edits only slightly better than without the numbers (+0.06 correlation).

title: weights_editing: replicating Sparks of Weight-Space Programming across LLMs
summary: Replicates the weight-editing experiments with several LLMs as the editor. The repository returned 404 on 2026-11-05.

title: OpenWSP
summary: An open replication with a Python kernel over weights, a forward-pass service and a versioned edit format (CLI, SDK and MCP server). Its own one-shot GPT-6 Astra rerun of the car repair failed (0/1,024, 2,918 weights changed).

title: WSPBench
summary: Does weight access help an agent diagnose and repair a model? GPT-6.1 Sol repaired 30/32 faults with behavior probes plus weights, against 14/32 with probes alone and 5/32 for a scripted solver at the same probe budget. All three kept 8 clean controls intact.

title: weightspace
summary: Apache-2.0 Python library: read, fix, write and improve any torch.nn.Module with an LLM, using budgeted probes, tracked edits and sparse patches. Its own rerun of the Qwen experiment did not beat the original edit.

title: weight-surgery
summary: Open agent skill that reads weights first, keeps a fixed forward-pass budget and proves fixes on held-out data. On a BERT NER model, a fitted control beat the hand edit (+0.109 vs +0.032 F1).

title: weight-space-programming-skill
summary: Claude Code skill for improving a small open LLM by editing its weights directly, with no training.

title: weights-lab
summary: Agent skill for editing LLM weights.

title: pi-weight-space-programming
summary: Extension for the Pi coding agent with skills for reading and editing weights.

title: weight-space-programming (agent skill)
summary: Agent skill for reasoning-driven weight inspection, targeted edits and small-network construction.

title: The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading
summary: Separates reading weights directly from repairing a model with code and practice feedback: raw-weight reading without tools appears only on the smallest networks, and the language-model results used Python and forward passes.

title: MIT team says GPT-6 Astra can improve other AI models by editing their weights. Critics say its biggest result relied on standard ML engineering.
summary: News coverage of the claims and the methodological pushback.

title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT (ROME)
authors: Kevin Meng, David Bau, Alex Andonian, Yonatan Belinkov
summary: Rank-one edits to a single MLP layer rewrite a stored fact.

title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer (MEMIT)
authors: Kevin Meng, Arnab Sen Sharma, Alex Andonian, Yonatan Belinkov, David Bau
summary: Extends ROME to thousands of edits at once across several layers.

title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
summary: Adding and subtracting fine-tuning weight differences (task vectors) steers a model's behavior.

title: Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering (ActAdd)
summary: Adds a direction computed from contrasting prompts to the residual stream at inference.

title: Representation Engineering: A Top-Down Approach to AI Transparency
summary: Reads and controls high-level concepts through population-level directions in representations.

title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA)
summary: Steering vectors from paired positive and negative examples shift behaviors such as sycophancy.

title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
summary: Orthogonalizing weights against one direction removes refusal. It is the same kind of edit as the Qwen loop fix.

title: Tracr: Compiled Transformers as a Laboratory for Interpretability
summary: Compiles RASP programs into transformer weights with known structure.

title: A Survey of Weight Space Learning: Understanding, Representation, and Generation
summary: Taxonomy of learning on weights: geometry and symmetries, weight embeddings, and weight generation.

title: Steering Robustness into World Action Models via Mechanistic Interpretability and Optimal Control (WA-LQR)
authors: Jihoon Hong, Julian Skifstad, Qi-Yu Dai, Alice Chan, Glen Chou
summary: Closed-loop LQR activation steering of Cosmos-Policy, DiT4DiT and LingBot-VA under camera, gripper and noise perturbations. Linear separability predicts which models can be steered.

title: Contrastive Conceptor Activation Steering (COAST): Unlocking Vision-Language-Action Models through Hidden States
authors: Miranda Muqing Miao, Subin Kim, Brandon Yang, Lyle Ungar
summary: Training-free conceptor steering of a VLA's action-expert residual stream (GR00T N1.5), learned from a few success and failure rollouts.

title: DiMaS: Distribution Matching for Steering Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: In flow-matching VLAs, behavioral features are linearly decodable but not linearly steerable, which motivates distribution matching instead.

title: Domain Arithmetic: One-Shot VLA Adaptation under Environmental Shifts (DART)
authors: Taewook Kang, Taeheon Kim, Donghyun Shin, Jonghyun Choi
summary: Adapts a VLA to camera and embodiment shifts from one demonstration through weight-vector arithmetic with subspace alignment.

title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning (WIZARD)
summary: A meta-network turns language and video into LoRA weights for a frozen VLA, with no test-time optimization.

title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
summary: Claude Opus 5.5 audited small head-and-neck planning-request screening networks (433 to 4,801 parameters) blind, without tools, data or code execution. It named the broken rule in 16 of 18 flawed networks and repaired each of the 16 by changing a median of 3 parameters. Checks used about 420,000 requests.

title: Weight-Space Programming (wsp-kit)
summary: Tool that tries to fix small open-weight models by editing weights directly, with an eval gate deciding whether an edit ships. Reports its own CPU runs on Qwen3-0.6B and GPT2-124M: in 60-item list-looping tests no edit passed the gate, so 0 weights shipped. Only the smoke-test pipeline passed (failing score 64.14 → 75.43).

title: Weight-Space Programming for the Social Safety Net
summary: Tests whether an LLM can write, with no training, the exact weights of small networks computing four simplified US benefit formulas (SNAP, EITC, SSI, Medicaid). Three of four match the formula to within a trillionth of a dollar; the EITC network differs at one point by 2.4 cents. Trained networks are off by dollars.

title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming — Complete Reproduction & Interactive Guide (EN / KO)
summary: Reproduction of all 8 experiments of the MIT report from the released weights, prompts and logs, with standalone NumPy/SciPy verification scripts. Reports max tensor difference 0.0 and a full run of about 3.5 seconds on CPU. Includes a bilingual (English/Korean) interactive web report and a separate Drosophila connectome weight-edit page.

title: Writing neural-network weights for Geister without training
summary: Claude Opus 5.5 agents write, read and fix neural-network weights for Geister, a two-player hidden-information game, without training. Compared with PPO and text-prompted small LMs, on an 8-core CPU machine. Repository includes per-item results (G1-G26), writer and reader run transcripts, audits, and an English summary and Japanese report.

title: Weight-space programming on a clinical splicing model
summary: Claude Opus 5.5 hand-edits 165 weights of OpenSpliceAI-MANE-10000nt to separate pathogenic from benign ClinVar variants. Hidden-test AUPRC 0.9385 → 0.9746. A temperature-only control gives 0.9695 and gradient fine-tuning of the same layers 0.9697-0.9710; authors conclude the edit matched ordinary training rather than beating it.

title: Can GPT-6 Astra read and write GPT-2's weights?
summary: Asks GPT-6 Astra to find induction heads in scrambled GPT-2 small (124M) weights. With Python and no hint it picked all five induction heads in both runs (10 of 10 picks); with no tools, 0 of 10. Silencing the five heads cuts repeat accuracy from 98.6% to 28.9%. One model, few runs, no size sweep.

title: Rethinking Weight-Space Programming
summary: Re-runs the report's experiments with baselines and controls. Tuned PPO reaches 99.2–114.4 on Seaquest vs Astra's 53.1. Unedited Qwen3.5-0.8B with thinking off scores 44.2% on MATH-500. A difference-of-means direction with no LLM reaches 41.9%. Without simulator source in the prompt, Seaquest median falls to 0.8.

title: Opus 5.5 makes π0.5 move faster and smoother by editing its weights
summary: Claude Opus 5.5, working in Claude Code from recorded rollouts, changed 1.16% of a Training-Time-RTC π0.5 for a real YAM bimanual robot. Bottle placement got 12.0% faster at 40 Hz and jumps between action chunks fell 89.8%; both policies kept 100% success (3 runs per condition). The edits were a RoPE intervention fitted into Q/K weights by least squares and a repair of a prefix-handling bug in official RTC. Project page only, no code or weights.
milestone: First Claude edit of a robot policy

title: Admiral: Muse Spark repairs a multi-agent RL policy by editing its weights
summary: Meta Muse Spark built a gated "steer home" circuit in a 163,874-parameter MAPPO capture-the-flag boat policy (PyQuaticus), changing 2.9% of weights. Against the hard heuristic opponent, paired score rose +0.36 over 200 held-out matches; against medium, +0.01 (not significant). Ships a reusable sandboxed numpy kernel with a match budget and a no-training audit.

title: Weight-space programming for F1TENTH autonomous racing
summary: GPT-6 Astra edited 1,276 scalars of a PPO LiDAR racing controller: completions went from 167 to 180 of 210 paired starts and crashes from 43 to 30. Runnable with a lock file and checkpoints.

title: Quadrotor PPO under actuation delay: LLM weight edits vs a gain sweep
summary: Two LLMs each made one blind edit to a PyBullet quadrotor policy. At 4 ms delay the original succeeds 5%, the LLM edits 16% and 12%, a 28-variant output-gain sweep 67% and retraining for 7M steps 61%; at 8 ms or more the LLM edits score 0–1%. A clear case of a scripted baseline beating the LLM edit.

title: wsp-lab: cross-editor stress test of weight-space programming
summary: An agentic GLM-5.3 editor repaired a CartPole MLP from 9.4 to 371.6 return, while a matched-norm random edit scored 9.5. Pre-registered, with an untouched baseline and a retraining upper bound; a blind Qwen3.5-0.8B repair gave no gain.

title: Reproducing Sparks of Weight-Space Programming with Claude Opus 5.5
summary: Claude Opus 5.5 repeats the Kinetix car repair at 1,024/1,024 episodes, changing 1.70% of weights, along with other experiments from the report.

title: Replication of Sparks of Weight-Space Programming with Claude Fable 5.1
summary: Claude Fable 5.1 repeats the Kinetix car repair at 1,024/1,024 episodes, changing 2.16% of weights, and the MinAtar experiments.

title: Weight-space Breakout pipeline and FailureIsAllYouNeed
summary: A hosted Qwen editor repairs injected faults in a 17,253-parameter Breakout policy behind a verifier gate, publishing accepted weights to Hugging Face. A useful negative result: the one accepted repair just restored the known reference policy, one run made 123 turns without submitting an edit, and a later qualified repair improved sampled play while greedy return fell from 10.25 to 1.57. Follow-up repo: FailureIsAllYouNeed.

title: Claude Fable 5.1 writes a Breakout network from scratch
summary: Fable 5.1 writes all 20,486 weights of a MinAtar Breakout policy in one reply and scores 501.6 ± 5.8, against 517.4 for Astra in the report.

title: Weight-space MinAtar: Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 write game policies
summary: Blind one-shot weight writing for MinAtar Breakout, Asterix and Seaquest. On Breakout, Fable 5.1 scores 533.9 and Opus 5.5 scores 7.1.

title: Weight-space horizon: re-evaluating the released MinAtar networks
summary: A pre-registered re-evaluation finds 51.6% of the released Breakout episodes still running at the 10K-step cap; a 30K cap adds 405.3 reward. Episode caps are a way to misread WSP scores.

title: OpenWiSH: Open Weight-Space Harness
summary: An agent-agnostic harness (claude -p, Codex or the Anthropic API) where agents inspect and edit weights through a Rust edit gate. Already runs Kinetix and MinAtar tasks.

title: RoboIRS: Inference-Time Internal Representation Steering for Generalist Robot Policies
authors: Lei, Liu, Li, Zhang, Liang, She et al.
summary: Linear classifiers on success and failure rollouts pick intervention sites and directions in frozen policies. π0.5 on 15 LIBERO-PRO tasks: 44.4% to 66.2%; Cosmos Policy: 35.4% to 55.4%. A plain diff-of-means direction already reaches 62.6% on π0.5, the baseline any agent edit has to beat.

title: Suppression Sticks, Locality Is Fragile: A Closed-Loop Audit of Task-Vector Negation in VLA Policies
authors: Wang, Guo, Dai, Zhao, Guo, Xiong
summary: Subtracting per-skill task vectors on 10 LIBERO-Goal skills: 5 are cleanly suppressed, 3 resist and 2 collapse the policy. Unrelated tasks keep only 52% of their success on average, and cosine between task vectors does not predict the outcome.

title: Behavioral Steering of Vision-Language-Action Models in the Low-Parameter Regime
summary: TinyLoRA adapters of 8 to 384 parameters on a frozen OpenVLA-OFT, trained by GRPO or gradient-free CMA-ES. With 256 parameters carry height rises 120 mm at 92% success. The closest tiny-weight-edit baseline for an agent edit.

title: Causal Analysis of Robot Foundation Models Enables Efficiency Gains
authors: Swann, Papillon, Jacobs, Boppana, Haklay, Bigelow et al.
summary: Activation patching on π0.5, MolmoAct2 and MolmoBot: information reaches the action expert through a narrow band of mid-to-late cross-attention layers, and patching there redirects which object is picked and where the arm moves. A map of where edits should land.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Interpretable and Steerable Features in VLA Models
summary: SAEs on π0.5 and OpenVLA: amplifying general features induces matching behavior and ablating them destroys performance, but most features are episode-specific memorization.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Steering Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Steering OpenVLA and π0 through FFN value vectors shifts end-effector motion on LIBERO by 27.7% on average; only the low and slow steers held up on hardware.

title: WeightLoop: Weight-Space Programming with Experimental Feedback
authors: Mengran Li, Bo Li, Weijing Zhao, Chengyang Zhang, et al.
summary: Framework in which GPT-6 Astra reads a task specification and model implementation, then writes a bounded parameter-editing program. The program turns experimental feedback into edits to a deployed predictor, with no further LLM calls or gradient retraining. In offline replay, targeted edits improve mean ranking utility in seven of eight endpoint-budget settings.

title: mraad/weight-space-programming
summary: Replicates Weight-Space Programming on Claude with no training. Claude names Breakout from raw weights (correct, 93% confidence; 60% with W1 rows shuffled). A Claude-written Breakout network scores 269.4 ± 7.4 (PPO 500M: 25.3, GPT-6 Astra: 517.4). In the Three Pads lander game, each Claude-written 484-weight network lands 3,000 of 3,000 flights.

title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"
summary: Tests Claude Opus 5.5 reading raw weights, given as plain text without tools, of ~125,000-parameter CNNs trained on five image datasets. Finds accurate local arithmetic but reliance on dataset priors: with CIFAR-10 labels permuted, every class pair the model interprets is wrong. Exploratory, mostly single runs; provides an auditing protocol.

title: IyadhKhalfallah/weight-space-programming
summary: Experiments editing and writing models without gradient descent, plus a wsl CLI that applies reversible weight patches with per-slice regression checks. A hand-written XGBoost model reached AUC 0.809 on rain forecasting with zero labels (0.839 when trained on 2.5 years). On a 0.8B LLM, the author's edit did not reproduce the published effect.

title: allthingssecurity/weight_space_programming
summary: Writes parameters of a randomly initialized model with the Qwen3.5-0.8B architecture directly, without gradient descent, to answer ABAP questions. Reports 18/25 correct in a small, unblinded static review, with random controls at 0/25. Includes 7 supplied-answer recall cases; not an expert ABAP model.

title: fderrigo/weight-space-programming-experiments
summary: Code, patches and results for two no-training edits chosen by Codex. Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Pinocchio fix changed 8.868% of values: target answers 0/24 to 11/24, with 7/8 original controls preserved. Qwen3-0.6B patch raised unauthorized tool calls on target requests from 1/40 to 13/40; selectivity incomplete.

title: sachgaur/WSP
summary: LeNet/MNIST pilot testing whether an agent can diagnose a failure from bounded numerical queries and repair it by editing the final classifier without training. Paired comparison of Astra and DeepSeek editors on fault and shortcut cases over seeds 42, 43 and 44, with a protocol fixed before evaluation.

title: Consistency Is Not Understanding: Orbit Audits for Neural Field Weight Readers
authors: Sungguk Cha, Mintae Kim, Youngsub Han, Byoung-Ki Jeon, Sangyeob Lee
summary: Tests whether readers recognize what shallow ReLU neural fields encode from their weights (480 shape fields, 1,000 MNIST fields), using hidden-neuron permutations and positive rescalings that leave the function unchanged. Compares statistics, set and language-model readers, with 1,920 scored reasoning-model sessions, and separates accuracy, agreement across transformed copies and disagreement on fresh identical prompts.

title: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity
org: U. Illinois College of Medicine / U. Chicago
summary: Proves that nets of threshold units with hand-chosen excitatory and inhibitory connections can realise any finite logical expression: the first networks whose weights are programmed by hand.

title: Representation of events in nerve nets and finite automata
summary: Proves that nets of threshold units are equivalent to finite automata and introduces regular expressions, the theoretical root of compiling automata into networks.

title: Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities
summary: Writes the weights of a symmetric recurrent network in one pass with the outer-product rule T_ij = Σ_s (2V_i^s−1)(2V_j^s−1) over the stored patterns, with no training.

title: "Neural" computation of decisions in optimization problems
summary: Derives a continuous Hopfield network's weights analytically from an energy function that encodes the Travelling Salesman Problem, with no learning. Moves from storing memories to compiling a task into the network.

title: Collective computational properties of neural networks: New learning mechanisms
authors: L. Personnaz, I. Guyon, G. Dreyfus
summary: Gives a closed-form pseudo-inverse rule, W = X X⁺, that computes the weights of an associative network directly from the patterns to be stored.

title: On the computational power of neural nets
summary: Proves, by explicit weight construction, that a finite recurrent network with rational weights simulates any Turing machine. Appeared at COLT 1992 and in the Journal of Computer and System Sciences in 1995.

title: A neural compiler
authors: F. Gruau, J.-Y. Ratajszczak, G. Wiber
summary: Presents a neural compiler that translates programs in a high-level, Pascal-like language into networks whose weights and topology are fully determined by the program.

title: Constructing deterministic finite-state automata in recurrent neural networks
summary: Gives a provably stable way to program a second-order recurrent network so that it implements any given deterministic finite-state automaton.

title: Thinking Like Transformers
summary: Proposes RASP, a programming language whose primitives map transformer-encoder attention and feed-forward computation. Provides RASP programs for histograms, sorting and Dyck-languages, relates task difficulty to required layers and heads, and shows a transformer can be trained to mimic a RASP solution.

title: Transformers Learn In-Context by Gradient Descent
summary: Gives a simple weight construction showing a single linear self-attention layer matches gradient descent on a regression loss. Shows empirically that self-attention-only Transformers trained on regression tasks match gradient-descent models or the construction's weights.

title: Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers
summary: Programs transformers with specific weights and places them in a loop, with the input sequence acting as a punchcard. Emulates a small instruction-set computer, mapping iterative algorithms to programs run by a looped, 13-layer transformer.

title: Non-Holographic Associative Memory
authors: D. J. Willshaw, O. P. Buneman, H. C. Longuet-Higgins
summary: Introduces a clipped outer-product associative memory whose connection matrix is written in one shot from the patterns to be stored, following Hebb's correlation rule.

title: Correlation Matrix Memories
summary: Presents a correlation-matrix memory whose matrix is written in one shot as a sum of outer products of the patterns to be stored.

title: Learning Transformer Programs
authors: Dan Friedman, Alexander Wettig, Danqi Chen
summary: Trains modified Transformers that are then converted into discrete, human-readable programs, building on RASP. Learns programs for in-context learning, sorting, Dyck languages, named entity recognition and text classification, performing on par with standard Transformers of comparable size.

title: What learning algorithm is in-context learning? Investigations with linear models
summary: Proves by construction that transformers can implement gradient descent and closed-form ridge regression for linear models. Shows trained in-context learners match gradient descent, ridge and least-squares predictors, with preliminary evidence of shared algorithmic features in late layers.

title: Connectionist expert systems
summary: Builds an expert system on a connectionist network (MACIE) and explains its conclusions by inspecting which weighted inputs determined each unit's output.

title: Medical diagnostic expert system based on PDP model
summary: Extracts if-then rules from a backpropagation network trained for medical diagnosis, at NTT. Presents a diagnostic expert system built on a parallel distributed processing model, with rules read from the trained network.

title: A distributed connectionist production system
summary: Implements rule matching and variable binding in a distributed connectionist production system, a network built to carry out symbolic rules.

title: Interpreting neural-network connection weights
summary: Proposes a weight-product measure of each input's importance, computed from the connection weights alone with no data.

title: Rule induction through integrated symbolic and subsymbolic processing
authors: C. McMillan, M.C. Mozer, P. Smolensky
summary: Describes RuleNet, which alternates learning with projecting the network's weights onto explicit rules and re-inserting those rules into the network.

title: Extraction, insertion and refinement of symbolic rules in dynamically driven recurrent neural networks
org: NEC Research Institute / RPI; OpenAlex lists U. Maryland and RPI
summary: Inserts known DFA transitions into second-order recurrent networks by programming a subset of weights to large values (±H), trains the network, then extracts refined automata by clustering hidden states, all in one paper.
history_milestone: Insert, refine, extract in one paper

title: Extracting refined rules from knowledge-based neural networks
summary: Extracts rules from trained knowledge-based networks by clustering weights and rewriting each unit as an 'M of these N antecedents' rule. Together with KBANN, it closes the knowledge-to-weights-to-knowledge loop.

title: Knowledge-based artificial neural networks
summary: Turns each propositional Horn clause into a unit whose weights (±ω) and bias are set analytically, adds low-weight links, then refines the network by backpropagation: a compiler from knowledge to weights.

title: Rule generation from neural networks
venue: IEEE Trans. Systems, Man, and Cybernetics
summary: Introduces the KT algorithm, which generates rules from a trained neural network by searching subsets of each unit's incoming weights.

title: Survey and critique of techniques for extracting rules from trained artificial neural networks
authors: R. Andrews, J. Diederich, A.B. Tickle
summary: Surveys techniques for extracting rules from trained networks and fixes the decompositional versus pedagogical taxonomy: read individual weights and units, or treat the network as a black box.

title: Extracting tree-structured representations of trained networks
summary: Extracts tree-structured representations (TREPAN) from trained networks by querying the network as an oracle rather than reading its weights.

title: The truth will come to light: directions and challenges in extracting the knowledge embedded within trained artificial neural networks
authors: A.B. Tickle, R. Andrews, M. Golea, J. Diederich
summary: Reviews directions and open challenges in extracting the knowledge embedded in trained neural networks, following the decompositional and pedagogical split.

title: Skeletonization: A technique for trimming the fat from a network via relevance assessment
summary: Introduces skeletonization, which assesses the relevance of units in a trained network and deletes the least relevant ones. The aim is a minimal network that is more interpretable.

title: Optimal brain damage
authors: Y. LeCun, J.S. Denker, S.A. Solla
summary: Ranks weights by a saliency computed from a diagonal approximation of the Hessian and deletes the lowest-ranked ones. Bell Labs authors present it as a way to prune trained networks.

title: A simple procedure for pruning back-propagation trained neural networks
summary: Proposes a simple procedure for pruning back-propagation trained networks by estimating the sensitivity of the error to each weight and removing low-sensitivity weights.

title: Creating artificial neural networks that generalize
summary: Studies how to build networks that generalize, pruning hidden units whose outputs are constant or duplicate other units.

title: Second order derivatives for network pruning: Optimal Brain Surgeon
org: Stanford University / Ricoh California Research Center
summary: Uses the full inverse Hessian to choose which weight to delete and to compute a closed-form update for all remaining weights. The update is commonly written δw = −(w_q/[H⁻¹]_qq) H⁻¹ e_q.

title: Pruning algorithms — a survey
summary: Surveys pruning algorithms for neural networks, from sensitivity-based weight removal to penalty terms, consolidating the field as of 1993.

title: Net2Net: Accelerating Learning via Knowledge Transfer
authors: Tianqi Chen, Ian Goodfellow, Jonathon Shlens
summary: Transfers the information in a trained network into a wider or deeper network through function-preserving transformations, so the new network starts with the same function. Reports a new state-of-the-art ImageNet accuracy after adding depth to Inception modules.

title: Network Morphism
authors: Tao Wei, Changhu Wang, Yong Rui, Chang Wen Chen
summary: Studies how to morph a trained network into a new one that completely preserves its function. Introduces network morphism equations and algorithms for changes of depth, width, kernel size and subnet, plus parametric activations for non-linearities.

title: Are Sixteen Heads Really Better than One?
authors: Paul Michel, Omer Levy, Graham Neubig
summary: Observes that a large percentage of attention heads can be removed at test time without significantly impacting performance, and some layers can be reduced to a single head. Also examines greedy pruning algorithms.

title: Optimal Brain Compression: A Framework for Accurate Post-Training Quantization and Pruning
summary: Introduces a framework covering weight pruning and quantization in the one-shot, post-training setting. It is built on an exact and efficient realization of the Optimal Brain Surgeon framework, extended to quantization.

title: SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can Be Accurately Pruned in One-Shot
summary: Prunes GPT-family models in one shot without retraining. Runs on OPT-175B and BLOOM-176B in under 4.5 hours, reaching 60% unstructured sparsity with negligible perplexity increase, ignoring more than 100 billion weights.

title: A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large Language Models (Wanda)
authors: Mingjie Sun, Zhuang Liu, Anna Bair, J. Zico Kolter
org: CMU, Meta AI, Bosch Center for AI
summary: Prunes pretrained LLMs by weight magnitude multiplied by input activation on a per-output basis. Requires no retraining or weight update, and is evaluated on LLaMA and LLaMA-2 against magnitude pruning.

title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
summary: Proposes that dense, randomly initialized networks contain subnetworks that reach comparable test accuracy when trained in isolation. Finds winning tickets under 10-20% of the size of fully-connected and convolutional networks on MNIST and CIFAR10.

title: The correlation theory of brain function
summary: Introduces dynamic links: synapses that change on a fast timescale to bind features temporarily, the earliest form of fast weights.

title: Learning to control fast-weight memories: An alternative to dynamic recurrent networks
summary: Describes a slow network that learns to output context-dependent weight changes for a second, fast network, so one net programs another net's weights on the fly. Offered as an alternative to dynamic recurrent networks.

title: A 'self-referential' weight matrix
summary: Adds special units that let a network address, read and modify any of its own weights, including the weights of the modification machinery itself, defining a self-referential weight matrix.

title: Goedel Machines: Self-Referential Universal Problem Solvers Making Provably Optimal Self-Improvements
summary: Presents self-referential problem solvers that rewrite any part of their own code once a proof searcher finds a proof the rewrite is useful. Shows such a self-rewrite is globally optimal, with no local maxima.

title: Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past
summary: Adds fast weights, variables that change slower than activities but faster than standard weights, as temporary memory of the recent past. Provides a neurally plausible form of attention to the past without storing copies of neural activity patterns.

title: Neural Network Quine
summary: Builds self-replicating neural networks that replicate by learning to output their own weights, trained with a loss function and a regeneration method. Also adds an MNIST classification task, observing a trade-off between classification and replication.

title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
authors: Imanol Schlag, Kazuki Irie, Jürgen Schmidhuber
summary: Shows the formal equivalence of linearised self-attention and early-1990s fast weight controllers, where a slow net programs another net's fast weights through additive outer products. Replaces additive updates with a delta-rule-like instruction and tests on retrieval, translation and language modelling.
history_milestone: Linear transformers equal fast weight programmers

title: A Modern Self-Referential Weight Matrix That Learns to Modify Itself
authors: Kazuki Irie, Imanol Schlag, Róbert Csordás, Jürgen Schmidhuber
summary: Proposes a scalable self-referential weight matrix that uses outer products and the delta update rule to modify itself during runtime. Evaluates it on supervised few-shot learning and multi-task reinforcement learning with procedurally generated game environments.

title: Eliminating Meta Optimization Through Self-Referential Meta Learning
summary: Investigates self-referential meta learning systems that modify themselves without explicit meta optimization. Proposes fitness monotonic execution, in which a network self-modifies on bandit and classic control tasks by receiving more computational resources when it performs better.

title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
summary: Makes the hidden state of a sequence layer a machine learning model, updated by a step of self-supervised learning even on test sequences. Evaluates TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP at 125M to 1.3B parameters against Transformer and Mamba.

title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
authors: Ali Behrouz, Peilin Zhong, Vahab Mirrokni
summary: Introduces a neural long-term memory module that learns to memorize historical context at test time, combined with attention in a family of three architecture variants. Reports scaling to context windows larger than 2M.

title: Training feedforward neural networks using genetic algorithms
summary: Applies a genetic algorithm directly to weight space, evolving real-valued weight genomes for a feedforward sonar classifier. It is one of the first uses of genetic algorithms to set network weights in 1989.

title: Genetic algorithms and neural networks: optimizing connections and connectivity
authors: D. Whitley, T. Starkweather, C. Bogart
summary: Uses the GENITOR genetic algorithm to optimize a network's weights and its connectivity together, treating both as a single search problem rather than training weights by gradient descent on a fixed topology.

title: Designing neural networks using genetic algorithms with graph generation system
org: Center for Machine Translation, CMU, and NEC Corporation, Tokyo
summary: Evolves graph-grammar rules with a genetic algorithm, and the rules emit the network's connectivity matrix. The search runs over programs that generate networks instead of over the networks themselves.

title: Automatic definition of modular neural networks
summary: Presents cellular encoding, which a thesis record calls a machine language for neural networks. It comes with a compiler from a high-level language, so evolution and explicit compilation share one representation.

title: Evolving artificial neural networks
summary: Reviews the field of evolving neural networks and gives a taxonomy that separates direct encodings from indirect encodings. It is published in Proceedings of the IEEE in 1999.

title: Evolving neural networks through augmenting topologies
summary: Introduces NEAT, a method that evolves connection weights and network topology together. It links the early neuroevolution work to the modern era.

title: Compositional pattern producing networks: A novel abstraction of development
summary: Introduces compositional pattern producing networks, small evolved networks that generate patterns; HyperNEAT later uses them to paint the weights of large, geometrically regular networks.

title: A Hypercube-Based Encoding for Evolving Large-Scale Neural Networks
authors: Kenneth O. Stanley, David B. D'Ambrosio, Jason Gauci
summary: Introduces HyperNEAT, a hypercube-based indirect encoding in which a small evolved network generates the weights of a large, geometrically regular network, used to evolve large-scale neural networks.

title: Evolving large-scale neural networks for vision-based reinforcement learning
authors: Jan Koutník, Giuseppe Cuccu, Jürgen Schmidhuber, Faustino Gomez
summary: Encodes a network of over 1M weights as a few DCT coefficients and evolves those coefficients. The resulting network learns to drive in the TORCS simulator directly from pixels.

title: Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning
summary: Tests Evolution Strategies, a black-box optimizer, as an alternative to MDP-based RL on MuJoCo and Atari. Communicating only scalars lets it scale to over a thousand workers, solving 3D humanoid walking in 10 minutes.

title: Deep Neuroevolution: Genetic Algorithms Are a Competitive Alternative for Training Deep Neural Networks for Reinforcement Learning
summary: Evolves DNN weights with a simple gradient-free genetic algorithm that performs well on Atari and humanoid locomotion. It evolves networks with over four million free parameters, the largest evolved with a traditional evolutionary algorithm.

title: Evolution Strategies at Scale: LLM Fine-Tuning Beyond Reinforcement Learning
summary: Applies evolution strategies to full-parameter fine-tuning of LLMs at the billion-parameter scale, without dimensionality reduction. The paper reports that it outperforms established RL implementations on several axes, including tolerance to delayed rewards and stability.

title: Predicting Parameters in Deep Learning
summary: Shows that a small set of weight values per feature can predict the remaining weights of several deep learning architectures. In the best case, more than 95% of a network's weights are predicted without any drop in accuracy.

title: HyperNetworks
authors: David Ha, Andrew M. Dai, Quoc V. Le
summary: Introduces hypernetworks, where one network generates the weights of another, trained end-to-end with backpropagation. Generates non-shared LSTM weights with near state-of-the-art sequence modelling results, and gives respectable image recognition results with fewer learnable parameters.

title: Dynamic Filter Networks
authors: Bert De Brabandere, Xu Jia, Tinne Tuytelaars, Luc Van Gool
summary: Introduces a layer whose convolution filters are generated dynamically from the input rather than fixed after training. Reaches state-of-the-art on moving MNIST with a much smaller model, and demonstrates video and stereo prediction.

title: Learning to learn by gradient descent by gradient descent
summary: Casts the design of an optimization algorithm as a learning problem, implementing learned optimizers with LSTMs. They outperform hand-designed competitors on trained tasks and generalize to new tasks with similar structure, including neural network training and neural art.

title: SMASH: One-Shot Model Architecture Search through HyperNetworks
authors: Andrew Brock, Theodore Lim, J. M. Ritchie, Nick Weston
summary: Trains an auxiliary HyperNet that generates the weights of a main model conditioned on its architecture. Validation performance of networks with generated weights ranks architectures at the cost of one training run, tested on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, ModelNet10 and Imagenet32x32.

title: Meta-Learning with Latent Embedding Optimization
summary: Learns a data-dependent latent generative representation of model parameters and performs gradient-based meta-learning in that low-dimensional latent space. Reports state-of-the-art few-shot classification on miniImageNet and tieredImageNet.

title: Graph HyperNetworks for Neural Architecture Search
authors: Chris Zhang, Mengye Ren, Raquel Urtasun
summary: Proposes a graph neural network hypernetwork that generates weights for a given architecture by inference over its topology. Random architectures scored with generated weights let search run nearly 10 times faster than other random search methods on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.

title: Parameter Prediction for Unseen Deep Architectures
authors: Boris Knyazev, Michal Drozdzal, Graham W. Taylor, Adriana Romero-Soriano
summary: Introduces the DeepNets-1M dataset of architecture graphs and a graph hypernetwork that predicts parameters in one forward pass. It predicts all 24 million parameters of a ResNet-50, reaching 60% accuracy on CIFAR-10.

title: HyperTransformer: Model Generation for Supervised and Semi-Supervised Few-Shot Learning
authors: Andrey Zhmoginov, Mark Sandler, Max Vladymyrov
summary: Uses a Transformer to generate the weights of a convolutional network directly from support samples for few-shot learning. For larger target models, generating only the last layer gives results competitive with or better than state-of-the-art methods.

title: Learning to Learn with Generative Models of Neural Network Checkpoints
summary: Trains a conditional diffusion transformer on a dataset of network checkpoints. Given initial parameters and a prompted loss, error or return, it predicts parameter updates achieving that metric, optimizing unseen parameters in one update.

title: VeLO: Training Versatile Learned Optimizers by Scaling Up
summary: Trains a small neural network optimizer that ingests gradients and outputs parameter updates, meta-trained with approximately four thousand TPU-months of compute. It needs no hyperparameter tuning; code, data and a benchmark suite are open-sourced.

title: Neural Network Diffusion
summary: Trains an autoencoder on a subset of trained network parameters, then a diffusion model on its latents, to synthesize new parameters. Generated models match or improve on trained networks across architectures and datasets, without memorizing them.

title: Editable Neural Networks
summary: Introduces Editable Training, a model-agnostic training technique that encourages fast editing of a trained model, patching a mistake on one sample without changing behavior on other samples. Tests it on large-scale image classification and machine translation.

title: Rewriting a Deep Generative Model
summary: Treats a layer of a deep generative model as a linear associative memory and derives an algorithm to modify one entry, changing a rule. Includes an interactive interface and outperforms fine-tuning and edit-transfer baselines on multiple datasets.

title: Editing Factual Knowledge in Language Models
authors: Nicola De Cao, Wilker Aziz, Ivan Titov
summary: Trains a hyper-network with constrained optimization to predict the weight update that changes one fact without affecting other knowledge. Tests it on a BERT fact-checking model and a BART question-answering model, with paraphrases changing consistently.

title: Editing a classifier by rewriting its prediction rules
summary: Presents a methodology for modifying a classifier's behavior by directly rewriting its prediction rules. Requires virtually no additional data collection and applies to adapting a model to new environments and ignoring spurious features.

title: Fast Model Editing at Scale
summary: Introduces MEND, small auxiliary editing networks that transform the fine-tuning gradient with a low-rank decomposition to make fast, local edits from one input-output pair. Trains on a single GPU in under a day for models of 10 billion+ parameters.

title: Knowledge Neurons in Pretrained Transformers
summary: Introduces a knowledge attribution method that identifies neurons expressing a relational fact in BERT on cloze tasks. Finds their activation correlates positively with the fact's expression, and case studies update and erase facts without fine-tuning.

title: Memory-Based Model Editing at Scale
summary: Introduces SERAC, which stores edits in an explicit memory and learns to reason over them to modulate the base model's predictions. Adds three editing problems on question answering, fact-checking and dialogue; only SERAC performs well on all three.

title: Does Localization Inform Editing? Surprising Differences in Causality-Based Localization vs. Knowledge Editing in Language Models
authors: Peter Hase, Mohit Bansal, Been Kim, Asma Ghandeharioun
summary: Shows that causal-tracing localization conclusions do not indicate which MLP layer is best to edit to override a stored fact. Also studies erasing and amplifying facts, where the edited layer predicts performance better than localization does.

title: Unified Concept Editing in Diffusion Models
summary: Presents UCE, which edits text-to-image diffusion models without training, using a closed-form solution on text-conditional projections. Demonstrates simultaneous debiasing, style erasure and content moderation, with improved efficacy and scalability over prior work.

title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
summary: Projects the perturbation of locate-then-edit methods onto the null space of preserved knowledge before applying it to parameters. Boosts most such methods by an average of 36.7% on LLaMA3, GPT2-XL and GPT-J with one added line of code.

title: GAN Dissection: Visualizing and Understanding Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: Presents a framework to visualize GANs at unit, object and scene level, identifying interpretable units tied to object concepts and measuring their causal effect through interventions. Locating and removing artifact-causing units improves GAN outputs.

title: Averaging Weights Leads to Wider Optima and Better Generalization
summary: Averages multiple points along the SGD trajectory with a cyclical or constant learning rate. Finds flatter solutions than SGD and approximates Fast Geometric Ensembling with one model. Improves test accuracy on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet across several architectures.

title: Loss Surfaces, Mode Connectivity, and Fast Ensembling of DNNs
summary: Shows that optima of deep network loss functions are connected by simple curves along which training and test accuracy stay nearly constant. Introduces a procedure to find them, and Fast Geometric Ensembling, which trains ensembles in the time of one model.

title: Linear Mode Connectivity and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
summary: Studies whether networks reach the same linearly connected minimum under different SGD noise. Finds vision models become stable early in training, and shows lottery-ticket subnetworks reach full accuracy only when stable: at initialization on MNIST, early in training on ImageNet.

title: Robust fine-tuning of zero-shot models
summary: Introduces WiSE-FT, which ensembles the weights of zero-shot and fine-tuned models such as CLIP. On ImageNet and five derived distribution shifts it improves shifted accuracy by 4 to 6 pp over prior work and ImageNet accuracy by 1.6 pp.

title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
summary: Averages the weights of multiple models fine-tuned with different hyperparameters, adding no inference or memory cost. The resulting ViT-G model attains 90.94% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, reported as a new state of the art.

title: Merging Models with Fisher-Weighted Averaging
summary: Frames merging as choosing parameters that maximize joint posterior likelihood, approximating each posterior as a Gaussian with Fisher information as precision. Improves on simple averaging and is competitive with gradient-based transfer learning at lower cost.

title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
summary: Introduces three algorithms that permute the hidden units of one model to align it with a reference model before merging in weight space. Demonstrates zero-barrier linear mode connectivity between independently trained ResNet models on CIFAR-10.

title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
summary: Introduces TIES-Merging, which resets parameters that changed little during fine-tuning, resolves sign conflicts, and merges only parameters agreeing with the chosen sign. Reports outperforming existing merging methods across modalities, domains, task counts, model sizes and architectures.

title: Language Models are Super Mario: Absorbing Abilities from Homologous Models as a Free Lunch
summary: Introduces DARE, which randomly drops delta parameters with ratio p and rescales the rest by 1/(1−p). Eliminates 90% or even 99% of SFT deltas, merges task-specific models, and yields a 7B model ranking first on the Open LLM Leaderboard.

title: Evolutionary optimization of model merging recipes
summary: Proposes an evolutionary search that automatically finds combinations of open-source models, in both parameter space and data flow space. Produces a Japanese Math LLM and a Japanese VLM, reporting state-of-the-art results on Japanese benchmarks.

title: Arcee's MergeKit: A Toolkit for Merging Large Language Models
summary: Introduces MergeKit, an open-source extensible library for merging language model parameters on any hardware. Reports that thousands of models have been merged by the community, including checkpoints assessed on the Open LLM Leaderboard.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
summary: Freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each Transformer layer. Compared with GPT-3 175B fine-tuned with Adam, it cuts trainable parameters 10,000 times and GPU memory 3 times, with on-par or better quality.

title: Implicit Self-Regularization in Deep Neural Networks: Evidence from Random Matrix Theory and Implications for Learning
authors: C. H. Martin, M. W. Mahoney
summary: Applies random matrix theory to layer weight matrices of pretrained and from-scratch networks, including AlexNet, Inception and LeNet5. Identifies 5+1 phases of training and a Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization form in state-of-the-art models.

title: Predicting Neural Network Accuracy from Weights
summary: Predicts a trained network's accuracy from simple weight statistics alone, ranking networks with R2 above 0.98. Releases 120k convolutional networks trained on four datasets; predictors transfer to unobserved datasets and architectures.

title: Classifying the classifier: dissecting the weight space of neural networks
summary: Trains meta-classifiers on weights to identify training-setup properties such as dataset, optimizer and architecture, using small subsets of consecutive weights. Releases the NWS dataset of 320K weight snapshots from 16K trained networks.

title: Predicting trends in the quality of state-of-the-art neural networks without access to training or testing data
authors: C. H. Martin, T. S. Peng, M. W. Mahoney
summary: Meta-analyzes hundreds of public pretrained models without training or test data. Finds norm-based metrics correlate with test accuracy, while power-law metrics from heavy-tailed self-regularization theory better separate well-trained from poorly-trained models.

title: Hyper-Representations: Self-Supervised Representation Learning on Neural Network Weights for Model Characteristic Prediction
summary: Learns representations of weights from populations of networks by self-supervised learning, with domain-specific augmentations and an adapted attention architecture. Recovers model characteristics and outperforms prior work predicting hyper-parameters, test accuracy and generalization gap.

title: From data to functa: Your data point is a function and you can treat it like one
summary: Treats data points as implicit neural representations called functa and proposes a framework for deep learning on them. Applies it to images, 3D shapes, NeRFs and manifold data for generation, imputation, view synthesis and classification.

title: Model Zoos: A Dataset of Diverse Populations of Neural Network Models
summary: Publishes 27 model zoos on eight image datasets, with 50,360 unique models plus sparsified twins, totaling over 3,844,360 model states. Provides analysis and benchmarks for studying weight-space structure across model populations.

title: Equivariant Architectures for Learning in Deep Weight Spaces
summary: Presents an architecture that takes an MLP's weights and biases as input, using layers equivariant to neuron-permutation symmetry. Characterizes all affine equivariant and invariant layers, built from pooling, broadcasting and fully connected operations.

title: Permutation Equivariant Neural Functionals
summary: Introduces permutation-equivariant neural functionals that process weights or gradients of MLPs and CNNs through NF-Layers with parameter sharing. Tasks include predicting generalization, producing winning-ticket sparsity masks, and classifying or editing implicit neural representations.

title: Graph Metanetworks for Processing Diverse Neural Architectures
summary: Represents input networks as graphs and processes them with graph neural networks. Handles attention, normalization, convolutional and ResNet blocks, proves expressivity and equivariance to parameter permutation symmetries, and validates on several metanetwork tasks.

title: Detecting Backdoors with Meta-Models
summary: Trains meta-models on about 4,000 clean and backdoored CNNs to detect backdoors from weights. Detects i.i.d.-trigger backdoors with over 99% accuracy.

title: Neural Decompiling of Tracr Transformers
summary: Generates a dataset of transformer-weight and RASP-program pairs with Tracr, then trains a model to recover RASP code from weights. Reproduces over 30% of test programs exactly; over 70% of outputs are functionally equivalent.

title: Visualizing and Understanding Convolutional Networks
summary: Introduces a technique that projects activations back to pixels, plus an ablation study of layers. The diagnosis yields an architecture outperforming Krizhevsky et al. on ImageNet, and it beats prior results on Caltech-101 and Caltech-256 after softmax retraining.

title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
summary: Claims that features connect into circuits by weights, and reads circuits directly from InceptionV1 weights. Opens the Distill Circuits thread from the OpenAI Clarity team in 2020, framing circuits as the unit of study.

title: Curve Circuits
summary: Reverse-engineers the curve detection algorithm and uses its ideas to craft an artificial neural network from scratch that reimplements it. The page does not say whether every weight was set by hand.

title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
summary: Shows that feed-forward layers act as key-value memories: keys correlate with textual patterns in training examples, and values induce output vocabulary distributions. Lower layers capture shallow patterns, upper layers more semantic ones; a layer's output composes its memories.

title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
summary: Defines QK circuits (W_E^T W_QK W_E) and OV circuits (W_U W_OV W_E) that can be read directly from weight matrices, and finds induction heads by reading composition between heads. Published by Anthropic in December 2021.

title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
summary: Finds induction heads, attention-head circuits that complete repeated patterns in context, by reading the composition between heads, and argues they drive much of in-context learning.

title: Toy Models of Superposition
summary: Explains polysemantic neurons through superposition, where a model represents more features than it has neurons. Anthropic work with Harvard collaborators, published in 2022 in the Transformer Circuits thread and as arXiv 2209.10652.

title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
summary: Explains how GPT-2 small performs indirect object identification with 26 attention heads in 7 main classes, found through causal interventions, and evaluates the explanation by faithfulness, completeness and minimality.

title: Analyzing Transformers in Embedding Space
summary: Interprets all parameters of a trained Transformer by projecting them into embedding space, with no forward or backward pass. Applications include aligning parameters across models and building a classifier without training by translating a fine-tuned classifier's parameters.
history_milestone: Weights read with zero forward passes

title: Progress Measures for Grokking via Mechanistic Interpretability
org: Nanda independent; Chan and Steinhardt at UC Berkeley
summary: Fully reverse engineers the algorithm small transformers learn for modular addition, which uses discrete Fourier transforms and trigonometric identities. Confirms it through activations, weights and ablations, and defines progress measures splitting training into memorization, circuit formation and cleanup.

title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
summary: Decomposes a one-layer transformer's MLP activations into thousands of interpretable features with sparse dictionary learning, giving a feature basis in place of individual neurons.

title: Interpretability in Parameter Space: Minimizing Mechanistic Description Length with Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition
summary: Introduces Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition, which splits a network's parameters into components that are faithful, minimal in number per input, and maximally simple. Identifies ground-truth mechanisms in toy settings; scaling to non-toy models remains open.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
summary: Trains sparse autoencoders to reconstruct language-model activations, learning sparsely activating features that are more interpretable and monosemantic than alternatives by automated measures. Pinpoints features causally responsible for counterfactual behavior on indirect object identification more finely than prior decompositions.

title: Network Dissection: Quantifying Interpretability of Deep Visual Representations
summary: Introduces a framework that scores individual hidden units of CNNs by their alignment with a dataset of semantic concepts, labelling units with objects, parts, scenes, textures, materials and colors. Compares networks across training tasks, initializations, depth, width, dropout and batch normalization.

title: Natural Language Descriptions of Deep Visual Features
summary: Introduces MILAN, which labels vision neurons with open-ended natural-language descriptions by searching for strings that maximize pointwise mutual information with the image regions where the neuron is active. Uses the descriptions to remove spurious-feature neurons.

title: Language Models Can Explain Neurons in Language Models
summary: Has GPT-4 explain each GPT-2 XL MLP neuron, simulate its activations from that explanation, and score the match. Releases explanations for 307,200 neurons, over 1,000 scoring at least 0.8; the method works worse on larger models and later layers.

title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
org: Independent research, UCL, Cambridge and others
summary: Automates circuit discovery by pruning computational-graph edges whose patching barely changes the output. Rediscovers 5/5 component types in GPT-2 Small's Greater-Than circuit, selecting 68 of 32,000 edges, all found manually before.

title: FIND: A Function Description Benchmark for Evaluating Interpretability Methods
summary: Introduces FIND, a benchmark of functions resembling neural-network components, with paired descriptions, for evaluating automated interpretability methods. Also presents an Automated Interpretability Agent that generates function descriptions interactively, and evaluates language-model description methods.

title: A Multimodal Automated Interpretability Agent
summary: Gives a pre-trained vision-language model tools to synthesize and edit inputs and compute maximally activating exemplars. Describes neurons comparably to expert human experimenters, reduces sensitivity to spurious features, and flags inputs likely to be misclassified.

title: Patchscopes: A Unifying Framework for Inspecting Hidden Representations of Language Models
summary: Introduces a framework in which a language model explains its own hidden representations in natural language. Treats prior vocabulary-projection and intervention methods as instances, and mitigates failures on early layers. Allows a larger model to explain a smaller one.

title: Automatically Interpreting Millions of Features in Large Language Models
summary: Builds an open-source pipeline using LLMs to generate and score natural-language explanations for SAE features, with five new, cheaper scoring techniques including intervention scoring. Finds SAE latents much more interpretable than neurons, including sparsified ones.

title: Auditing Language Models for Hidden Objectives
summary: Trains a language model with a hidden objective of exploiting RLHF reward-model errors, then runs a blind auditing game with four teams. Three teams uncover the objective, using SAE interpretability, behavioral attacks and training data analysis.

title: Building and Evaluating Alignment Auditing Agents
summary: Builds alignment auditing agents, including a Claude Sonnet 4 investigator using SAE tools and steering. It solves the auditing game about 13% of the time, 42% with super-agent aggregation; interpretability tools raise win rates by roughly 10–20 points.

title: Learning to Interpret Weight Differences in Language Models
summary: Introduces Diff Interpretation Tuning, which trains an adapter on synthetic labeled weight diffs so a finetuned model describes its own finetuning-induced changes. Demonstrates it on reporting hidden behaviors and summarizing finetuned knowledge.

title: Evolution through Large Models
summary: Uses a code-generating LLM as the mutation operator in genetic programming, combined with MAP-Elites. Produces hundreds of thousands of Python programs for ambulating robots in Sodarace, then uses them to train a conditional model that outputs walkers for a terrain.

title: HyperTuning: Toward Adapting Large Language Models without Back-propagation
authors: Jason Phang, Yi Mao, Pengcheng He, Weizhu Chen
summary: Trains a T5-based hypermodel, HyperT5, to generate soft prefixes or LoRA parameters for a frozen T5 model from few-shot examples, without backpropagation at adaptation. Evaluated on P3, MetaICL and Super-NaturalInstructions, it generates parameters for unseen tasks.

title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
summary: Places an LLM inside an evolutionary loop where it proposes program mutations and an automated evaluator scores them. The system finds new cap-set constructions. Published in Nature by Google DeepMind authors.

title: Large Language Models as Optimizers
summary: Prompts an LLM with earlier solutions and their scores so it generates new ones. Tested on linear regression, traveling salesman and prompt optimization; best prompts beat human-designed ones by up to 8% on GSM8K and up to 50% on Big-Bench Hard.

title: Large Language Models As Evolution Strategies
authors: Robert Tjarko Lange, Yingtao Tian, Yujin Tang
summary: Prompts an LLM zero-shot with sorted, discretized population members and asks it to propose an improved mean, forming an evolution strategy. It outperforms random search and Gaussian Hill Climbing on synthetic BBOB functions and small neuroevolution tasks.

title: Transformer-Squared: Self-adaptive LLMs
authors: Qi Sun, Edoardo Cetin, Yujin Tang
summary: Adapts an LLM at inference in two passes: a dispatch system identifies task properties, then expert vectors trained with reinforcement learning, acting on singular components of weight matrices, are mixed. Reports outperforming LoRA with fewer parameters, including on vision-language tasks.

title: NeuroGen: Neural Network Parameter Generation via Large Language Models
authors: Jiaqi Wang, Yusen Zhang, Xi Li
summary: Generates neural network parameters with an LLM in two stages: pretraining on network checkpoints, then instruction tuning with prompts describing data, task and architecture. Reports that it generates usable network parameters.

title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
summary: Keeps an archive of coding agents, samples one, and has a foundation model produce a modified version that rewrites its own code. Each change is validated on coding benchmarks rather than proved, and SWE-bench performance increases.

title: Text-to-LoRA: Instant Transformer Adaption
authors: Rujikorn Charakorn, Edoardo Cetin, Yujin Tang, Robert Tjarko Lange
summary: Trains a hypernetwork to construct LoRA adapters for an LLM in one forward pass from a natural-language task description. Trained on 9 pre-trained LoRAs, its reconstructed adapters match task-specific adapters on test sets and generalize zero-shot to unseen tasks.

title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
summary: Orchestrates LLMs in an evolutionary pipeline that improves algorithms by directly changing code, using feedback from evaluators. Applied to Google data-center scheduling and mathematics problems, it found a procedure multiplying two 4×4 complex matrices using 48 scalar multiplications.

title: Self-Adapting Language Models
summary: Has an LLM generate its own self-edits, meaning finetuning data and update directives, applied through supervised finetuning as persistent weight updates. A reinforcement learning loop rewards self-edits by downstream performance; tested on knowledge incorporation and few-shot generalization.

title: Drag-and-Drop LLMs: Zero-Shot Prompt-to-Weights
summary: Maps a handful of unlabeled task prompts to LoRA matrices using a text encoder and a hyper-convolutional decoder. Reports up to 12,000× lower overhead than full fine-tuning and average gains up to 30% over trained LoRAs on unseen benchmarks.

title: Fault Injection Attack on Deep Neural Network
authors: Yannan Liu, Lingxiao Wei, Bo Luo, Qiang Xu
summary: Shows that faults injected into a network's parameters can force misclassification, including a single bias attack that changes one bias term.

title: Bit-Flip Attack: Crushing Neural Network with Progressive Bit Search
authors: Adnan Siraj Rakin, Zhezhi He, Deliang Fan
summary: Proposes an attack that flips a few bits in DRAM-stored weights, using Progressive Bit Search that combines gradient ranking and progressive search. Drops ResNet-18 top-1 accuracy from 69.8% to 0.1% with 13 flips out of 93 million bits.

title: Terminal Brain Damage: Exposing the Graceless Degradation in Deep Neural Networks Under Hardware Fault Attacks
summary: Studies bitwise corruptions on 19 DNN models across six architectures and three image tasks. Finds most models have at least one parameter whose bit-flip causes over 90% accuracy loss; Rowhammer drops accuracy up to 99%.

title: Weight Poisoning Attacks on Pre-trained Models
authors: Keita Kurita, Paul Michel, Graham Neubig
summary: Constructs weight poisoning attacks in which pre-trained weights carry backdoors that appear after fine-tuning, triggered by a keyword. Uses a regularization method called RIPPLe and an initialization called Embedding Surgery, tested on sentiment, toxicity and spam tasks.

title: An Embarrassingly Simple Approach for Trojan Attack in Deep Neural Networks
summary: Proposes a training-free trojan attack that inserts a tiny trojan module into a target model without changing the original parameters. Reports 100% attack success rate without affecting original-task accuracy, and evades state-of-the-art trojan detection algorithms.

title: Handcrafted Backdoors in Deep Neural Networks
authors: Sanghyun Hong, Nicholas Carlini, Alexey Kurakin
summary: Introduces a handcrafted backdoor attack that directly manipulates a model's weights instead of poisoning training data. Keeps attack success rate above 96% across four datasets and four architectures, and evades many backdoor detection and removal defenses.

title: Planting Undetectable Backdoors in Machine Learning Models
authors: Shafi Goldwasser, Michael P. Kim, Vinod Vaikuntanathan, Or Zamir
summary: Shows how a malicious learner can plant a backdoor that no computationally bounded observer can detect without the key. Gives a digital-signature construction for any model and a white-box undetectable construction for Random Fourier Features and random ReLU networks.

title: Data-free Backdoor Removal based on Channel Lipschitzness
authors: Runkai Zheng, Rongjun Tang, Jianze Li, Li Liu
summary: Defines a Channel Lipschitz Constant and computes an upper bound directly from weight matrices. Prunes channels with high values to remove backdoors without data, reporting state-of-the-art results among mainstream defense methods.

title: BadEdit: Backdooring Large Language Models by Model Editing
summary: Formulates backdoor injection as a lightweight knowledge editing problem that directly alters a subset of LLM parameters. Needs 15 samples, reaches up to 100% attack success rate, and the backdoor survives later fine-tuning.

title: Assessing the Brittleness of Safety Alignment via Pruning and Low-Rank Modifications
summary: Identifies safety-critical regions in LLMs through pruning and low-rank modifications, finding them sparse: about 3% at the parameter level and 2.5% at the rank level. Removing them compromises safety without significantly reducing utility.

title: PrisonBreak: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with at Most Twenty-Five Targeted Bit-flips
summary: Jailbreaks safety-aligned LLMs by flipping 5 to 25 targeted bits in parameters, using a bit-selection algorithm. Reaches 80-98% attack success on 10 open-source LLMs, and 69-91% on 5 models in a GDDR6 Rowhammer demonstration.

title: Reluplex: An Efficient SMT Solver for Verifying Deep Neural Networks
summary: Presents an SMT-based technique that extends the simplex method to handle ReLU activations, verifying properties of deep networks or giving counter-examples. Tested on ACAS Xu collision-avoidance networks, it proves properties of networks an order of magnitude larger than prior methods.

title: Parameter Space Noise for Exploration
summary: Adds noise directly to an agent's parameters rather than to its actions to drive exploration. Tested with DQN, DDPG and TRPO, it learns more efficiently than action-space noise and evolutionary strategies alone.

title: Simple random search provides a competitive approach to reinforcement learning
authors: Horia Mania, Aurelia Guy, Benjamin Recht
summary: Introduces a random search method for training static linear policies for continuous control. It matches state-of-the-art sample efficiency on MuJoCo locomotion tasks and is at least 15 times more computationally efficient than the fastest competing model-free methods.

title: Verifiable Reinforcement Learning via Policy Extraction
authors: Osbert Bastani, Yewen Pu, Armando Solar-Lezama
summary: Trains decision-tree policies guided by a DNN oracle and its Q-function, combining model compression with imitation learning. The trees are verified on Pong variants and cart-pole, and match the original DNN policy's performance.

title: Verisig: Verifying Safety Properties of Hybrid Systems with Neural Network Controllers
summary: Converts sigmoid-based neural network controllers into equivalent hybrid systems, then checks closed-loop safety with reachability tools. Shows reachability is decidable for one-hidden-layer networks, and for general networks if Schanuel's conjecture holds. Evaluated in two case studies.

title: Dota 2 with Large Scale Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Trains OpenAI Five with self-play RL over 10 months and beats the Dota 2 world champions; over twenty offline surgeries change the live policy's architecture while preserving its function.

title: Neural Network Surgery with Sets
authors: Jonathan Raiman, Susan Zhang, Christy Dennison
summary: Formalizes surgery, the transfer of trained weights between networks across feature and architecture changes. Uses discrete feature sets and set operations to determine automatically which components to keep and which to retrain, validated on the OpenAI Five model.

title: Weight Agnostic Neural Networks
summary: Searches for network architectures that perform tasks without weight training, evaluating each with a single shared weight sampled from a uniform distribution. Finds minimal networks solving reinforcement learning tasks, and MNIST networks with accuracy well above chance.

title: Efficient Representation and Approximation of Model Predictive Control Laws via Deep Learning
summary: Shows that ReLU networks can exactly represent the piecewise affine function from model predictive control of linear time-invariant systems. Gives bounds on the minimum layers and neurons required, and illustrates smaller memory needs through simulation examples.

title: Rapidly Adaptable Legged Robots via Evolutionary Meta-Learning
summary: Combines evolutionary-strategies meta-learning with a Batch Hill-Climbing adaptation operator to adapt robot policies to changed dynamics. On a quadruped, it adapts the policy using less than 3 minutes of real data.

title: Reincarnating Reinforcement Learning: Reusing Prior Computation to Accelerate Progress
summary: Proposes reincarnating RL, a workflow where prior computation such as learned policies is reused across design iterations or agents. Proposes an algorithm for transferring a sub-optimal policy to a value-based agent, tested on Atari 2600, locomotion and stratospheric balloon navigation.

title: Editing Large Language Models: Problems, Methods, and Opportunities
summary: Surveys model editing for LLMs, defining the task and its challenges, empirically comparing leading methods, and introducing a new benchmark dataset to evaluate editing techniques and guide method selection for specific tasks.

title: Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Reviews knowledge-based model editing for LLMs, formalizing the problem and organizing methods in a taxonomy based on how new knowledge is introduced, then covering metrics, datasets, and applications.

title: A Comprehensive Study of Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
summary: Reviews knowledge editing approaches for LLMs under a three-group categorization: using external knowledge, merging knowledge into the model, and editing intrinsic knowledge. Adds the KnowEdit benchmark for empirical evaluation and an analysis of knowledge location.

title: A Survey on Knowledge Editing of Neural Networks
summary: Reviews knowledge editing for neural networks, formalizing the problem in a common framework, distinguishing it from continual learning, and surveying the main editing approaches and datasets proposed so far.

title: Trends in Integration of Knowledge and Large Language Models: A Survey and Taxonomy of Methods, Benchmarks, and Applications
summary: Reviews how knowledge is integrated into LLMs through knowledge editing and retrieval augmentation, presenting a taxonomy of methods, benchmarks, and applications, along with analysis of methods and future research directions.

title: Knowledge Mechanisms in Large Language Models: A Survey and Perspective
summary: Reviews knowledge mechanisms in LLMs through a taxonomy of knowledge utilization (memorization, comprehension and application, creation) and knowledge evolution in individual and group models, and discusses the fragility of parametric knowledge and potential dark knowledge.

title: Editing the Mind of Giants: An In-Depth Exploration of Pitfalls of Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models
summary: Surveys side effects of knowledge editing in LLMs, such as knowledge distortion and loss of general abilities, re-evaluating methods with consistent metrics and benchmarks and reviewing related work and research directions.

title: Editing Across Languages: A Survey of Multilingual Knowledge Editing
authors: Nadir Durrani, Basel Mousi, Fahim Dalvi
summary: Surveys multilingual knowledge editing, organizing methods into parameter-based, memory-based, fine-tuning, and hypernetwork approaches, and reviewing benchmarks, transfer findings, cross-lingual propagation challenges, and open problems including language anisotropy, evaluation coverage, and edit scalability.

title: A Dual-Axis Taxonomy of Knowledge Editing for LLMs: From Mechanisms to Functions
summary: Introduces a taxonomy of knowledge editing for LLMs along two axes: editing mechanism and the function of edited knowledge, spanning factual, temporal, conceptual, commonsense, and social knowledge, plus problem definition, evaluation tasks, and datasets.

title: Bring Your Own Knowledge: A Survey of Methods for LLM Knowledge Expansion
summary: Surveys methods for expanding LLM knowledge across factual information, domain expertise, language proficiency, and user preferences, covering continual learning, model editing, and retrieval-based adaptation, and discussing knowledge consistency and scalability challenges.

title: On Knowledge Editing in Federated Learning: Perspectives, Challenges, and Future Directions
summary: Surveys knowledge editing, covering augmentation and removal, in federated learning, proposing a Federated Editable Learning paradigm across the FL lifecycle, placing existing methods within it, and outlining challenges and future directions.

title: Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
authors: Ningyu Zhang, Yunzhi Yao, Shumin Deng
summary: Presents a tutorial on knowledge editing for large language models, serving as an introduction to the topic of modifying what a model knows after it has been trained.

title: Editing Large Language Models
summary: Presents a three-hour tutorial on editing large language models, introducing the practice of modifying the behavior and knowledge of an already trained model.

title: Emptying the Ocean with a Spoon: Should We Edit Models?
summary: Argues that direct model editing cannot be trusted as a systematic remedy for LLM factual errors, contrasting it with retrieval-based architectures, concept erasure, and attribution methods, and calls for cautious, limited use.

title: Fundamental Problems With Model Editing: How Should Rational Belief Revision Work in LLMs?
