summary: Critiques the standard formulation of model editing as belief revision, describing 12 open problems in problem definition, benchmarks, and editable beliefs, and proposes a semi-synthetic Wikidata testbed evaluated against an idealized Bayesian agent.

title: Position: Editing Large Language Models Poses Serious Safety Risks
summary: Argues that editing LLMs poses overlooked safety risks, citing malicious use cases, ecosystem vulnerabilities, and low institutional awareness, and calls for tamper-resistant models, countermeasures, and securing the AI ecosystem.

title: Unveiling the Pitfalls of Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
summary: Investigates side effects of knowledge editing in LLMs using new benchmark datasets and metrics, identifying knowledge conflict from logically clashing edits and knowledge distortion of the model's innate knowledge structure.

title: The Mirage of Model Editing: Revisiting Evaluation in the Wild
summary: Revisits model editing evaluation with the QAEdit benchmark and WILD framework, showing that single-edit performance drops from 96.8% to 38.5% under realistic testing and that sequential editing fails drastically at 1000 edits.

title: Is Model Editing Built on Sand? Revealing Its Illusory Success and Fragile Foundation
summary: Argues that reported model editing success is illusory, with editors exploiting shortcuts instead of semantics, and introduces new evaluation methods showing state-of-the-art approaches collapse even under simple negation queries.

title: Continual Learning for Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Surveys continual learning for LLMs through a multi-stage categorization of continual pretraining, instruction tuning, and alignment, contrasting it with simpler adaptation, retrieval-augmented generation, and model editing, and discussing benchmarks, challenges, and future directions.

title: Towards Lifelong Learning of Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Surveys lifelong learning for LLMs, splitting strategies into internal knowledge (continual pretraining and finetuning) and external knowledge (retrieval-based and tool-based), with a taxonomy of 12 scenarios and emerging techniques like model expansion and data selection.

title: Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey
summary: Surveys knowledge conflicts in LLMs across three categories: context-memory, inter-context, and intra-memory conflict, examining their causes, model behaviors under conflict, and available solutions for improving robustness.

title: Model Merging in LLMs, MLLMs, and Beyond: Methods, Theories, Applications and Opportunities
summary: Surveys model merging across methods, theories, and applications, proposing a taxonomy of merging methods and covering use in LLMs, multimodal LLMs, and over ten machine learning subfields, with challenges and future directions.

title: Deep Model Fusion: A Survey
summary: Surveys deep model fusion in four categories: mode connectivity, alignment, weight averaging, and ensemble learning, and analyzes challenges of fusing large-scale models such as high computational cost and interference between heterogeneous models.

title: Merge, Ensemble, and Cooperate! A Survey on Collaborative Strategies in the Era of Large Language Models
summary: Surveys collaborative strategies for LLMs, categorized into merging in parameter space, ensembling model outputs, and cooperation among models for specific tasks, and discusses motivations, applications, and future research directions.

title: A Survey on Model MoErging: Recycling and Routing Among Specialized Experts for Collaborative Learning
summary: Surveys methods that recycle specialized expert models through routers, proposing a taxonomy of key design choices and suitable applications. Also inventories software tools and applications, and relates MoErging to model merging, multitask learning, and mixture-of-experts.

title: Deep Model Merging: The Sister of Neural Network Interpretability -- A Survey
summary: Surveys model merging through the lens of loss landscape geometry, distilling four characteristics: mode convexity, determinism, directedness, and connectivity. Argues these insights apply to interpretability and robustness, and proposes research directions at their intersection.

title: From Task-Specific Models to Unified Systems: A Review of Model Merging Approaches
summary: Reviews model merging methods, establishing a new taxonomy and systematically comparing approaches, motivated by inconsistent terminology and settings where training data is inaccessible. Aims to give newcomers a structured overview of key developments.

title: Model Merging in the Era of Large Language Models: Methods, Applications, and Future Directions
summary: Surveys merging of fine-tuned LLMs through the FUSE taxonomy of foundations, unification strategies, scenarios, and ecosystem. Covers weight averaging, task vector arithmetic, sparsification, mixture-of-experts, evolutionary optimization, applications, tools, and benchmarks.

title: From Parameters to Behaviors: A Survey of Model Fusion for Large Language Models
summary: Defines model fusion for LLMs and organizes prior work into parameter-level, representation-level, and behavior-level fusion. Also reviews metrics, benchmarks, applications, challenges, and future directions.

title: A Short Survey of Averaging Techniques in Stochastic Gradient Methods
summary: Surveys averaging techniques in stochastic gradient optimization, from the theory of Polyak–Ruppert averaging to tail averaging, exponential moving averages, and stochastic weight averaging. Covers modern developments, machine learning applications, finite-sample results, and open problems.

title: A Survey on LoRA of Large Language Models
summary: Reviews LoRA for large language models, categorizing progress into downstream adaptation variants, cross-task generalization by mixing multiple LoRA plugins, efficiency improvements, federated privacy-preserving methods, and applications. Also discusses future directions.

title: Low-Rank Adaptation for Foundation Models: A Comprehensive Review
summary: Reviews low-rank adaptation for foundation models beyond LLMs, covering technique foundations, emerging frontiers, and applications across multiple domains. Discusses challenges in theoretical understanding, scalability, and robustness.

title: A Unified Study of LoRA Variants: Taxonomy, Review, Codebase, and Empirical Evaluation
summary: Presents a unified study of LoRA variants, categorizing them along four axes: rank, optimization dynamics, initialization, and mixture-of-experts integration. Adds a theoretical review, a modular codebase, and a large-scale evaluation across language and image tasks.

title: Harnessing Multiple Large Language Models: A Survey on LLM Ensemble
summary: Reviews LLM ensemble methods, introducing a taxonomy and classifying approaches as ensemble-before-inference, ensemble-during-inference, or ensemble-after-inference. Also covers benchmarks, applications, and future research directions.

title: Taxonomy, Opportunities, and Challenges of Representation Engineering for Large Language Models
summary: Surveys representation engineering for LLMs, which manipulates internal representations to control behavior, framing it as a pipeline of representation identification, operationalization, and control. Compares strengths and weaknesses, identifies challenges, and offers best-practice guidance.

title: Representation Engineering for Large-Language Models: Survey and Research Challenges
summary: Formalizes the goals and methods of representation engineering, which uses contrasting inputs to detect and edit high-level concept representations in LLMs. Compares it with mechanistic interpretability, prompt engineering, and fine-tuning, outlines risks, and sets a research agenda.

title: Controllable Text Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Reviews controllable text generation for LLMs, dividing tasks into content control and attribute control. Covers retraining, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, prompt engineering, latent space manipulation, and decoding-time intervention, plus evaluation, applications, and challenges.

title: A Survey on Training-free Alignment of Large Language Models
summary: Reviews training-free alignment of LLMs, categorizing methods by pre-decoding, in-decoding, and post-decoding stages, examined for both LLMs and multimodal LLMs. Identifies key challenges and future directions.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
summary: Surveys concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models, categorizing methods as fine-tuning for parameter updates, closed-form edits, or inference-time interventions, and by the architectural components they modify. Also covers adversarial attacks, defenses, datasets, metrics, and benchmarks.

title: Erasing Concepts, Steering Generations: A Comprehensive Survey of Concept Suppression
authors: Yiwei Xie, Ping Liu, Zheng Zhang
summary: Surveys concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models, organizing approaches along intervention level, optimization structure, and semantic scope. Discusses evaluation benchmarks, metrics, datasets, trade-offs, and future directions such as adversarial robustness.

title: Rethinking Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
summary: Explores machine unlearning for LLMs across conceptual formulation, methodologies, metrics, and applications, highlighting unlearning scope, data-model interaction, and multifaceted efficacy assessment. Connects it to model editing and influence functions, and outlines an assessment framework.

title: Knowledge Unlearning for LLMs: Tasks, Methods, and Challenges
summary: Surveys knowledge unlearning for LLMs, defining the problem and categorizing methods into parameter optimization, parameter merging, and in-context learning. Presents evaluation datasets and concludes with ongoing challenges and future directions.

title: Digital Forgetting in Large Language Models: A Survey of Unlearning Methods
summary: Surveys digital forgetting in LLMs, covering background, motivations, desired properties, and a detailed taxonomy of machine unlearning methods. Also details datasets, models, and metrics for evaluating forgetting, retention, and runtime, and discusses challenges.

title: Machine Unlearning in Generative AI: A Survey
summary: Surveys machine unlearning in generative AI, spanning language and vision generative models, with a new problem formulation, evaluation methods, and structured discussion of the advantages and limitations of different technique types. Presents challenges and directions.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Machine Unlearning Techniques for Large Language Models
summary: Surveys machine unlearning for LLMs, introducing definitions, paradigms, and a taxonomy of existing studies. Categorizes approaches by strengths and limitations, reviews evaluation metrics and benchmarks, and outlines future research directions.

title: A Survey on Unlearning in Large Language Models
summary: Reviews over 180 papers on LLM unlearning published since 2021, with a taxonomy by pipeline phase separating parameter modification from parameter selection. Analyzes evaluation, comparing 18 benchmarks and dividing memorization metrics into 10 categories.

title: SoK: Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
summary: Proposes an intention-oriented taxonomy of LLM unlearning, distinguishing true removal of internal knowledge from suppression of behavioral effects. Examines evaluation limitations and practical challenges such as scalability and sequential unlearning.

title: Unlearning in LLMs: Methods, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
summary: Surveys unlearning methods for LLMs, categorized as data-centric, parameter-centric, architecture-centric, hybrid, and other strategies. Reviews benchmarks, metrics, and datasets, and outlines open problems including efficiency, formal guarantees, multimodal unlearning, and adversarial relearning.

title: Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models: Foundations, Advances, and Agentic Extensions
summary: Compares machine unlearning methods, benchmarks, and evidence across LLMs and systems with retrieval, memory, tools, and agents. Organizes them with a five-layer framework, seven-stage lifecycle, and six evidence dimensions, and argues current evidence is insufficient to establish removal.

title: The Frontier of Data Erasure: Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
summary: Reviews machine unlearning for large language models, presenting methods for targeted forgetting without full retraining. Divides existing research into unlearning from unstructured textual data and from structured classification data, and discusses challenges in preserving model integrity.

title: Machine Unlearning for Traditional Models and Large Language Models: A Short Survey
summary: Surveys machine unlearning for traditional models and LLMs, covering definitions, classification, evaluation criteria and challenges in different settings. Categorizes unlearning for each model type and proposes ways to measure effectiveness and efficiency.

title: Right to be Forgotten in the Era of Large Language Models: Implications, Challenges, and Solutions
summary: Examines how data-erasure rights under the GDPR challenge LLM-based systems, which store and process information differently from search engine indexes. Discusses technical solutions including differential privacy, machine unlearning, model editing and guardrails.

title: Preserving Privacy in Large Language Models: A Survey on Current Threats and Solutions
summary: Surveys privacy threats to LLMs, reviewing privacy attacks and the memorization of sensitive information. Organizes solutions along the learning pipeline, from dataset anonymization to differential privacy during training or inference and machine unlearning after training.

title: Multimodal Unlearning Across Vision, Language, Video, and Audio: Survey of Methods, Datasets, and Benchmarks
summary: Surveys unlearning in multimodal foundation models across vision, language, audio and video, offering a system-oriented view. Provides a taxonomy comparing architectures and modalities by trade-offs among deletion strength, retention, efficiency, reversibility and robustness, and notes open problems.

title: Generative Model Unlearning: A Survey through Target Events, Unlearning Operators, and Evaluation Protocols
summary: Reviews generative model unlearning by formulating it as target-constrained distributional projection, where a target event, an unlearning operator and evidence on suppression, preservation and cost define a request. Reorganizes prior studies under this view.

title: Machine Unlearning Doesn't Do What You Think: Lessons for Generative AI Policy and Research
summary: Argues that machine unlearning does not deliver what policy discussions expect for generative AI, offering a framework for researchers and policymakers. Identifies mismatches between unlearning goals, removing information from parameters or suppressing it in outputs, and feasible implementations.

title: Position: LLM Unlearning Benchmarks are Weak Measures of Progress
summary: Argues that LLM unlearning benchmarks give an overly optimistic view of method effectiveness. Shows through simple benign modifications to popular benchmarks that supposedly unlearned information remains accessible or retained performance degrades, and recommends cautious interpretation and better future practice.

title: Open Problems in Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
summary: Identifies open problems in using machine unlearning for AI safety, focusing on dual-use knowledge in domains such as cybersecurity and CBRN. Covers side effects of removing dangerous knowledge, tensions with existing safety mechanisms, and challenges in evaluation and robustness.

title: Eight Methods to Evaluate Robust Unlearning in LLMs
summary: Surveys techniques and limitations of existing LLM unlearning evaluations, then applies a set of robustness tests to the Who's Harry Potter model. Finds extractable knowledge, comparable latent representations and collateral unlearning, arguing for comprehensive rather than ad-hoc evaluation.

title: Position: The Term "Machine Unlearning" Is Overused in LLMs
summary: Argues that "machine unlearning" is overused in LLM research and should be reserved for dataset-defined deletion approximating retraining without a specified forget set. Contends that refusal, entity removal and suppression need different terminology and evaluations matching their objectives.

title: Is your algorithm unlearning or untraining?
summary: Argues that "unlearning" is overloaded across two problem formulations, distinguishing untraining, which reverses the influence of a forget set, from unlearning, which removes the broader underlying concept or behaviour. Gives technical definitions and maps literature settings to each.

title: Position: Bridge the Gaps between Machine Unlearning and AI Regulation
summary: Argues that machine unlearning's usefulness for AI regulation depends on researchers closing gaps between current methods and applications, using the EU AI Act as a case study. Catalogs potential compliance applications and flags the technical gaps for each.

title: A Survey of Machine Unlearning
summary: Surveys machine unlearning's concepts, scenarios, methods and applications, motivated by right-to-be-forgotten regulation. Covers formulations, design criteria, removal requests and algorithms, and highlights current trends and new research areas.

title: Towards Reliable Forgetting: A Survey on Machine Unlearning Verification
summary: Surveys methods for verifying machine unlearning, proposing a taxonomy of behavioral verification and parametric verification based on the type of evidence used. Examines assumptions, strengths and limitations of representative methods, identifies deployment vulnerabilities, and lists open problems.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety -- A Review
summary: Reviews mechanistic interpretability for AI safety, which reverse engineers network computations into human-understandable algorithms and concepts. Covers foundational concepts such as features, methodologies for causally dissecting behavior, benefits and risks, and challenges of scalability and automation.

title: Toward Transparent AI: A Survey on Interpreting the Inner Structures of Deep Neural Networks
summary: Reviews over 300 works on inner interpretability of deep neural networks. Organizes methods by which network part they explain (weights, neurons, subnetworks or latent representations) and whether they are intrinsic or post hoc, and links interpretability to adjacent fields.

title: Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability
summary: Discusses, as a forward-facing review, the frontier of mechanistic interpretability and its open problems, spanning conceptual and practical improvements to methods, applying them to specific scientific and engineering goals, and socio-technical challenges.

title: A Primer on the Inner Workings of Transformer-based Language Models
summary: Introduces techniques for interpreting the inner workings of Transformer-based language models, focusing on decoder-only architectures. Overviews known internal mechanisms these models implement, with connections across popular approaches and active research directions.

title: A Practical Review of Mechanistic Interpretability for Transformer-Based Language Models
summary: Surveys mechanistic interpretability for transformer-based language models from a task-centric perspective, organizing its taxonomy around research questions. Outlines objects of study, techniques, evaluation methods and key findings for each task, as a roadmap for newcomers.

title: The Quest for the Right Mediator: Surveying Mechanistic Interpretability Through the Lens of Causal Mediation Analysis
summary: Surveys mechanistic interpretability through causal mediation analysis, taxonomizing the field by the types of causal units (mediators) used and the methods for searching over them. Discusses pros and cons of each and recommends new mediators and standardized evaluations.

title: Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability
summary: Presents causal abstraction as a theoretical foundation for mechanistic interpretability, generalizing it to arbitrary mechanism transformation and formalizing concepts such as polysemantic neurons and the linear representation hypothesis. Unifies methods including activation patching, circuit analysis, sparse autoencoders and steering.

title: Locate, Steer, and Improve: A Practical Survey of Actionable Mechanistic Interpretability in Large Language Models
summary: Surveys mechanistic interpretability as an intervention methodology for LLMs, structured as a pipeline of localizing, steering and improving. Categorizes diagnosis and intervention methods by interpretable object and covers gains in alignment, capability and efficiency.

title: Mechanistic?
summary: Distinguishes four uses of the term "mechanistic" in interpretability research, from a narrow causal-claim definition to a broad cultural one. Traces the history of the NLP interpretability community and the mechanistic community, arguing the polysemy reflects a divide.

title: The Cognitive Revolution in Interpretability: From Explaining Behavior to Interpreting Representations and Algorithms
summary: Grounds mechanistic interpretability in cognitive science, arguing for a shift from explaining behavior to interpreting representations, echoing psychology's move beyond behaviorism. Proposes a taxonomy of semantic interpretation (learned representations) and algorithmic interpretation (operations over them).

title: Position: An Inner Interpretability Framework for AI Inspired by Lessons from Cognitive Neuroscience
summary: Proposes a conceptual framework for building mechanistic explanations in AI inner interpretability, drawing lessons from cognitive neuroscience, and gives concrete methodological strategies to address recent critiques of the field.

title: Explaining AI through mechanistic interpretability
venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science
summary: Offers a philosophy-of-science account of explanation in mechanistic interpretability, treating the field's results as explanations of how AI systems work.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs Philosophy
summary: Argues that mechanistic interpretability needs ongoing engagement with philosophy to clarify concepts, refine methods and handle epistemic and ethical complexities, illustrating this with three open problems from the MI literature.

title: Make Mechanistic Interpretability Auditable: A Call to Develop Guidelines via Continuous Collaborative Reviewing
summary: Argues that mechanistic interpretability lacks standardized auditing and calls for continuous collaborative reviewing, expert-verified guidelines and protocols, and source-based systems that track the arguments on which claims depend.

title: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Must Disclose Identification Assumptions for Causal Claims
summary: Argues that mechanistic interpretability papers should disclose identification assumptions behind causal claims, based on audits of 10 papers across four methodological strands and then 30 papers, and proposes a disclosure norm.

title: How to use and interpret activation patching
summary: Provides advice and best practices for applying activation patching, covering the different ways to apply it, how to interpret results as evidence about circuits, and the choice of metric and its pitfalls.

title: An introduction to graphical tensor notation for mechanistic interpretability
summary: Introduces graphical tensor notation and applies it first to decompositions such as SVD, CP, Tucker and tensor networks, then to foundational approaches for understanding language models, ending with an induction head circuit example.

title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
summary: Lays out a foundational agenda for the circuits research programme, framing neural network understanding around features, circuits and universality.

title: A Survey on Sparse Autoencoders: Interpreting the Internal Mechanisms of Large Language Models
summary: Surveys sparse autoencoders for interpreting LLMs, covering their architecture, design improvements and training strategies, input-based and output-based feature explanation methods, structural and functional evaluation metrics, and applications to understanding and manipulating model behavior.

title: Sparse Autoencoders for Mechanistic Interpretability in NLP: A Critical Survey of Recoverability, Interpretability, and Utility
summary: Surveys 138 studies on sparse autoencoders in NLP, proposing a task-grounded taxonomy that links dictionary design, feature operations and NLP functions, and assessing evidence on recoverability, interpretability, faithfulness and behavioral utility.

title: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Should Prioritize Feature Consistency in SAEs
summary: Argues that SAE research should prioritize feature consistency across training runs, proposes the PW-MCC metric to measure it, and reports that TopK SAEs reach high consistency on LLM activations with suitable architectural choices.

title: Position: Use Sparse Autoencoders to Discover Unknowns
summary: Argues that sparse autoencoders are less effective for acting on known concepts but well suited to discovering unknown ones, a distinction that reconciles negative and positive results, and outlines use cases in interpretability, safety, and social and health sciences.

title: Interpreting Language Models Through Concept Descriptions: A Survey
summary: Surveys methods that use generator models to produce natural-language concept descriptions of neurons, attention heads and SAE features, covering generation methods, automated and human evaluation metrics, and underlying datasets. Identifies a need for more rigorous causal evaluation.

title: A Survey on the Linear Representation Hypothesis
summary: Analyzes inconsistencies in how the linear representation hypothesis is treated across AI, neuroscience and cognitive science, and proposes a formalization that makes dependencies on model, representation location, feature definition and evaluation dataset explicit, plus open problems.

title: Attention Heads of Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Surveys the roles of attention heads in LLMs through a four-stage framework of Knowledge Recalling, In-Context Identification, Latent Reasoning and Expression Preparation, and divides discovery methods into Modeling-Free and Modeling-Required, alongside evaluation methods and benchmarks.

title: A Survey on Mechanistic Interpretability for Multi-Modal Foundation Models
summary: Surveys mechanistic interpretability for multimodal foundation models, including contrastive and generative vision-language models and text-to-image models, covering adaptation of LLM interpretability methods and mechanistic differences from unimodal models, organized in a structured taxonomy of methods.

title: Towards a Mechanistic Understanding of Large Reasoning Models: A Survey of Training, Inference, and Failures
summary: Surveys the mechanistic understanding of large reasoning models, organizing findings into training dynamics, reasoning mechanisms and unintended behaviors, and discusses under-explored challenges including applied interpretability, improved methodologies and a unified theoretical framework.

title: A Review of Developmental Interpretability in Large Language Models
summary: Reviews developmental interpretability in LLMs, moving from static post-hoc analysis to studying training itself, covering probing, causal tracing and circuit analysis, circuit formation, emergent abilities as phase transitions, parallels with human development, safety implications and open challenges.

title: Attention Sink in Transformers: A Survey on Utilization, Interpretation, and Mitigation
summary: Surveys attention sink in Transformers, where attention concentrates on a few uninformative tokens, organizing research into fundamental utilization, mechanistic interpretation and strategic mitigation.

title: Interpretability in Activation Space Analysis of Transformers: A Focused Survey
summary: Reviews interpretability methods that examine the activation space formed by neuron activations in transformer feed-forward layers, discussing each work in detail and pointing to future research directions given limited existing research.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Understanding Language Abilities in Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Surveys mechanistic interpretability work on language abilities in LLMs, covering probing, neuron-level and circuit-level analysis, and causal interventions used to study linguistic competence.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Large Language Model Alignment: Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions
summary: Reviews mechanistic interpretability for LLM alignment, covering techniques such as circuit discovery, feature visualization, activation steering and causal intervention, along with progress, challenges and future directions.

title: Neuron-level Interpretation of Deep NLP Models: A Survey
authors: Hassan Sajjad, Nadir Durrani, Fahim Dalvi
summary: Surveys neuron-level analysis of deep NLP models, covering methods to discover and understand neurons, evaluation methods, major findings including cross-architecture comparisons, applications such as controlling models and domain adaptation, and open issues.

title: Probing Classifiers: Promises, Shortcomings, and Advances
summary: Reviews the probing classifiers framework, in which a classifier predicts linguistic properties from model representations, and critically examines its promises, methodological shortcomings and advances.

title: Analysis Methods in Neural Language Processing: A Survey
summary: Surveys analysis methods for neural language processing models, categorizing them by prominent research trends, and highlights existing limitations and potential directions for future work.

title: A Primer in BERTology: What we know about how BERT works
authors: Anna Rogers, Olga Kovaleva, Anna Rumshisky
summary: Surveys over 150 studies of BERT, covering what information the model learns and how it is represented, modifications to training objectives and architecture, overparameterization, and compression approaches, before outlining future research directions.

title: Interpreting Deep Learning Models in Natural Language Processing: A Review
summary: Reviews interpretation methods for neural NLP models, organized into training-based, test-based, and hybrid approaches, with sub-categories such as influence-function, KNN-based, attention-based, saliency-based, and perturbation-based methods, and points out deficiencies and future directions.

title: Post-hoc Interpretability for Neural NLP: A Survey
authors: Andreas Madsen, Siva Reddy, Sarath Chandar
summary: Categorizes recent post-hoc interpretability methods for neural NLP by how they communicate explanations to humans, discusses each method in depth, and examines how the explanations are validated.

title: Towards Faithful Model Explanation in NLP: A Survey
authors: Qing Lyu, Marianna Apidianaki, Chris Callison-Burch
summary: Reviews over 110 NLP model explanation methods through the lens of faithfulness, covering its definition and evaluation, and groups approaches into five categories: similarity-based, model-internal structure analysis, backpropagation-based, counterfactual intervention, and self-explanatory models.

title: Explainability for Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Introduces a taxonomy of explainability techniques for Transformer-based language models, split by fine-tuning and prompting paradigms, with local and global explanations in each, plus evaluation metrics, uses for debugging, and open challenges.

title: From Understanding to Utilization: A Survey on Explainability for Large Language Models
summary: Surveys explainability for pre-trained Transformer LLMs, classifying methods into local and global analyses, then covering uses in model editing, controlled generation, and model enhancement, along with evaluation metrics and datasets.

title: Towards Uncovering How Large Language Model Works: An Explainability Perspective
summary: Reviews how knowledge is composed in LLM parameters via mechanistic interpretability and embedded in representations via probing and representation engineering, then examines training dynamics such as grokking and memorization and applications to editing, pruning, and alignment.

title: Rethinking Interpretability in the Era of Large Language Models
summary: Argues that LLMs offer an opportunity to redefine interpretability with broader scope, including auditing LLMs; reviews evaluation of both interpreting LLMs and using LLMs for explanation, and highlights dataset analysis and interactive explanations as priorities.

title: Usable XAI: 10 Strategies Towards Exploiting Explainability in the LLM Era
summary: Introduces 10 strategies for using explainability with LLMs, covering how XAI can explain and improve LLM-based systems and how LLMs can improve XAI techniques, with key techniques and associated challenges for each.

title: XAI meets LLMs: A Survey of the Relation between Explainable AI and Large Language Models
summary: Surveys the relation between XAI and LLM research, examining two paths, improving performance through XAI and interpreting models, and covering both peer-reviewed and arXiv preprint papers while advocating balanced progress in both fields.

title: LLMs for Explainable AI: A Comprehensive Survey
authors: Ahsan Bilal, David Ebert, Beiyu Lin
summary: Surveys approaches that use LLMs to turn complex model outputs into understandable narratives, covering evaluation techniques for LLM-generated explanations, challenges and limitations, real-world applications, and future directions.

title: Towards Transparent AI: A Survey on Explainable Large Language Models
summary: Reviews explainability techniques for LLMs categorized by transformer architecture (encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder), then covers their evaluation, practical applications, available resources, open challenges, and future directions.

title: Explainable and Interpretable Multimodal Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
summary: Surveys interpretability and explainability of multimodal LLMs, proposing a framework that categorizes research by data, model, and training and inference, and analyzing token-level to embedding-level representations, architecture analysis and design, and transparency-enhancing strategies.

title: A Survey on Neural Network Interpretability
summary: Reviews neural network interpretability research, clarifying definitions and proposing a three-dimensional taxonomy by engagement type (passive versus active), explanation type, and local-to-global focus, then summarizes evaluation methods and research directions.

title: On Interpretability of Artificial Neural Networks: A Survey
summary: Reviews studies on understanding the mechanisms of neural networks under a comprehensive taxonomy, describes applications of interpretability especially in medicine, and discusses future directions such as links to fuzzy logic and brain science.

title: Methods for Interpreting and Understanding Deep Neural Networks
authors: Grégoire Montavon, Wojciech Samek, Klaus-Robert Müller
summary: Introduces techniques for interpreting deep neural networks and explaining their predictions as an entry-level tutorial, with theory, practical tricks, recommendations for use on real data, and a discussion of applications.

title: Visual Interpretability for Deep Learning: a Survey
summary: Reviews studies on understanding CNN representations and learning interpretable, disentangled middle-layer representations, covering visualization, diagnosis of pre-trained CNNs, disentanglement, middle-to-end learning, and prospective trends in explainable AI.

title: A Survey Of Methods For Explaining Black Box Models
summary: Classifies the main problems addressed in black-box explanation literature by the notion of explanation and the type of black box system, helping researchers find relevant proposals and placing open research questions in perspective.

title: Explaining Explanations: An Overview of Interpretability of Machine Learning
summary: Defines explainability and uses that definition to classify existing interpretability literature, discusses why current explanatory methods for deep neural networks are insufficient, and suggests future research directions for explanatory AI.

title: Explainable Deep Learning: A Field Guide for the Uninitiated
summary: Offers a field guide for newcomers to explainable deep learning, introducing three dimensions that define foundational methods, discussing evaluation of explanations, relating explainability to adjacent research areas, and covering user-oriented explanation design and future directions.

title: Concept-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence: A Survey
summary: Reviews concept-based explainable AI methods, defining concepts and explanation types, presenting a taxonomy of nine categories with guidelines for choosing one, and reporting common evaluation strategies including metrics, human evaluations, and datasets.

title: Explainability of Vision Transformers: A Comprehensive Review and New Perspectives
summary: Reviews explainability methods for vision transformers, organizing them in a taxonomy by motivations, structures, and application scenarios, and covering evaluation criteria, tools and frameworks, unexplored aspects, and future research directions.

title: The Mythos of Model Interpretability
summary: Examines the diverse and sometimes discordant motivations for interpretability and the model properties and techniques thought to confer it, contrasting transparency with post-hoc explanation and questioning claims that linear models are interpretable while deep networks are not.

title: Towards A Rigorous Science of Interpretable Machine Learning
summary: Argues for a more rigorous science of interpretable machine learning by defining interpretability, describing when it is needed, suggesting a taxonomy for rigorous evaluation, and exposing open questions.

title: Interpretability Needs a New Paradigm
summary: Argues that interpretability should explore new paradigms while staying vigilant about faithfulness, examining the intrinsic and post-hoc paradigms and presenting three emerging ones: easily measurable faithfulness, optimized faithful explanations, and joint prediction-and-explanation models.

title: Rule Extraction from Recurrent Neural Networks: A Taxonomy and Review
summary: Reviews methods for extracting finite-state machines and rules from recurrent neural networks, organizing them within a taxonomy of extraction approaches.

title: Using neural networks for data mining
authors: Mark W. Craven, Jude W. Shavlik
summary: Surveys approaches that make trained neural networks comprehensible through rule extraction, focusing on the TREPAN-era methods used in data mining.

title: Neuro-fuzzy rule generation: survey in soft computing framework
summary: Surveys fuzzy-rule extraction and generation from neural and neuro-fuzzy models, treating how rule bases are obtained from such networks within a soft computing framework.

title: Rule extraction from support vector machines: A review
summary: Reviews rule extraction from support vector machines, a model family adjacent to neural networks, and reuses the ADT taxonomy to categorize the extraction approaches.

title: Rule Extraction from Support Vector Machines
summary: Collects edited chapters on rule extraction from support vector machines, covering methods for deriving comprehensible rules from trained SVM models.

title: Rule extraction from neural networks — A comparative study
summary: Compares existing rule-extraction methods for neural networks side by side, contrasting how the approaches differ and perform, without proposing a new method.

title: Rule Extraction Algorithm for Deep Neural Networks: A Review
summary: Reviews rule extraction algorithms for deep neural networks, classifying them as decompositional, pedagogical or eclectic and evaluating them by the network structure each targets, and finds limited study of deep-network extraction.

title: Extracting Relational Explanations From Deep Neural Networks: A Survey From a Neural-Symbolic Perspective
authors: Joe Townsend, Thomas Chaton, João M. Monteiro
summary: Surveys work connecting rule extraction with neural-symbolic integration, covering how relational explanations can be obtained from deep neural networks.

title: Rule-Extraction Methods From Feedforward Neural Networks: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Sara El Mekkaoui, Loubna Benabbou, Abdelaziz Berrado
summary: Reviews systematically the rule-extraction methods for feedforward neural networks, covering two decades of approaches mostly suited to shallow networks with recent developments for deep learning, limited to supervised learning and crisp rules.

title: Combining Symbolic and Neural Learning
summary: Surveys approaches that combine symbolic and neural learning, giving an overview of how the two paradigms are integrated.

title: Knowledge-Based Neurocomputing
summary: Compiles an edited volume of chapters on knowledge-based neural computing, addressing how knowledge is combined with neural network models.

title: Neural-Symbolic Learning Systems: Foundations and Applications
authors: Artur S. d'Avila Garcez, Krysia B. Broda, Dov M. Gabbay
summary: Introduces the CILP approach of translating logic programs into neural networks, alongside knowledge extraction, as a book-length treatment of neural-symbolic learning foundations and applications.

title: Dimensions of Neural-symbolic Integration — A Structured Survey
venue: We Will Show Them! Essays in Honour of Dov Gabbay
summary: Surveys neural-symbolic integration, covering how connectionist systems handle symbolic knowledge and the logics involved, and classifies systems by their architectures and abilities along several dimensions.

title: Perspectives of Neural-Symbolic Integration
summary: Collects edited chapters on neural-symbolic integration, spanning approaches to combining connectionist learning with symbolic knowledge representation and reasoning.

title: Neural-Symbolic Cognitive Reasoning
authors: Artur S. d'Avila Garcez, Luís C. Lamb, Dov M. Gabbay
summary: Presents a book-length treatment of reasoning in neural-symbolic systems, combining connectionist learning with logic for cognitive reasoning and learning.

title: Neural-Symbolic Learning and Reasoning: A Survey and Interpretation
summary: Surveys neural-symbolic learning and reasoning through the views of several researchers, in three parts: scope and theoretical foundations, systems and applications, and challenges with directions for future research.

title: Neural-Symbolic Computing: An Effective Methodology for Principled Integration of Machine Learning and Reasoning
summary: Surveys recent neural-symbolic computing work as a principled way to integrate machine learning and reasoning, outlining the methodology's main characteristics and its role in building explainable, accountable AI systems.

title: Neurosymbolic AI: The 3rd Wave
authors: Artur d'Avila Garcez, Luís C. Lamb
summary: Relates early and recent neurosymbolic research that integrates neural learning with symbolic knowledge representation and logical reasoning, drawing on 20 years of work to identify key ingredients and challenges for the next decade.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence: Current Trends
summary: Provides a structured overview of current neuro-symbolic AI trends by categorizing recent publications from key conferences, intended as a starting point for research on the topic.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence: The State of the Art
summary: Compiles an edited volume of chapters presenting the state of the art in combining symbolic methods with neural networks.

title: Neuro-symbolic approaches in artificial intelligence
summary: Gives an overview of neuro-symbolic approaches in AI, describing how they combine neural network learning with symbolic methods and representations.

title: The Third AI Summer: AAAI Robert S. Engelmore Memorial Lecture
summary: Presents a memorial lecture laying out an agenda for AI's third summer, and is the origin of a six-type taxonomy of neural-symbolic system designs.

title: A Survey on Neural-symbolic Learning Systems
summary: Surveys neural-symbolic learning systems, which combine neural perception with symbolic cognition, from four perspectives: challenges, methods, applications and future directions.

title: From Statistical Relational to Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence: a Survey
summary: Surveys the integration of learning and reasoning in neurosymbolic and statistical relational AI, characterizing systems along seven shared dimensions such as logical inference, syntax, semantics, learning scope, representations and learning tasks.

title: Towards Data-and Knowledge-Driven Artificial Intelligence: A Survey on Neuro-Symbolic Computing
authors: Wenguan Wang, Yi Yang, Fei Wu
summary: Provides a systematic overview of neuro-symbolic computing, from its history and background to a categorization of recent approaches by neural-symbolic integration, knowledge representation, knowledge embedding and functionality, with applications, benchmarks on three tasks and open problems.

title: Neurosymbolic AI and its Taxonomy: a survey
summary: Surveys recent research on models that combine symbolic processing with neural networks, presented as a route toward AGI beyond scaling data and model size. Classifies and compares the models and their applications.

title: Neuro-Symbolic AI in 2024: A Systematic Review
summary: Reviews neuro-symbolic AI research from 2020 to 2024 using the PRISMA methodology, analyzing 167 papers selected from 1,428 candidates. Maps coverage across learning, reasoning, knowledge representation, explainability and meta-cognition, and identifies gaps.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence: A Task-Directed Survey in the Black-Box Models Era
authors: Giovanni Pio Delvecchio, Lorenzo Molfetta, Gianluca Moro
summary: Surveys task-specific advances in neuro-symbolic methods, especially in natural language processing and computer vision, examining how symbolic systems can improve explainability and reasoning. Provides reproducibility details and per-paper comments in an accompanying repository.

title: Informed Machine Learning -- A Taxonomy and Survey of Integrating Knowledge into Learning Systems
summary: Introduces a taxonomy of approaches that integrate prior knowledge into machine learning, classifying them by knowledge source, representation, and integration point in the pipeline. Surveys papers covering representations such as algebraic equations, logic rules and simulation results.

title: A review of some techniques for inclusion of domain-knowledge into deep neural networks
summary: Reviews ways of injecting prior domain knowledge into deep networks, grouped by whether the knowledge alters the inputs, the loss, or the model.

title: Position: Weight Space Should Be a First-Class Generative AI Modality
authors: Zhangyang Wang, Peihao Wang, Kai Wang
summary: Argues that model checkpoints should be treated as a first-class data modality and that generative modeling in weight space should become a core primitive. Organizes existing methods into a five-stage pipeline, surveys practical applications, and clarifies current limits.

title: Model Lakes
authors: Koyena Pal, David Bau, Renée J. Miller
summary: Introduces the concept of model lakes, inspired by data lakes, for finding, differentiating and understanding collections of deep learning models. Formalizes tasks including attribution, versioning, search and benchmarking, and discusses research challenges and applicable data management techniques.

title: Symmetry in Neural Network Parameter Spaces
authors: Bo Zhao, Robin Walters, Rose Yu
summary: Surveys symmetries in neural network parameter spaces, meaning transformations that leave the network function unchanged, and how they shape loss landscapes and learning dynamics. Summarizes the literature, links symmetry to learning theory, and identifies gaps.

title: Learning from models beyond fine-tuning
summary: Reviews methods that adapt foundation models through the model interface without access to raw training data, grouped into five areas: model tuning, distillation, reuse, meta learning and model editing. Closes with open issues and future directions.

title: Where Do We Stand with Implicit Neural Representations? A Technical and Performance Survey
summary: Reviews implicit neural representation methods, which model data as continuous functions using multilayer perceptrons, under a taxonomy of activation functions, position encoding, combined strategies and network structure optimisation. Includes an experimental comparison across tasks and discusses limitations.

title: Implicit Neural Representation in Medical Imaging: A Comparative Survey
summary: Surveys implicit neural representation models in medical imaging, covering reconstruction, segmentation, registration, novel view synthesis and compression. Discusses advantages, limitations, data-related challenges and future directions, and compiles cited studies with open-source implementations.

title: A Brief Review of Hypernetworks in Deep Learning
summary: Reviews hypernetworks, which generate weights for a target network, and categorizes them by five design criteria: inputs, outputs, variability of inputs and outputs, and architecture. Covers applications across deep learning problem settings and open challenges.

title: Dynamic Neural Networks: A Survey
summary: Reviews dynamic networks that adapt their structure or parameters to each input, divided into instance-wise, spatial-wise and temporal-wise categories. Covers architecture design, decision-making schemes, optimization techniques, applications and open problems.

title: Learning to Optimize: A Primer and A Benchmark
summary: Presents the first comprehensive survey and benchmark of learning to optimize for continuous optimization, setting up taxonomies and categorizing existing works and directions. Benchmarks many approaches on representative problems and releases the Open-L2O software package.

title: Learning to optimize: A tutorial for continuous and mixed-integer optimization
authors: Xiaohan Chen, Jialin Liu, Wotao Yin
summary: Introduces learning-to-optimize techniques that use machine learning to accelerate optimization algorithms, estimate solutions quickly, or reshape the problem itself. Considers prerequisites for successful application and problem structure, as a guide for practitioners and researchers.

title: Tutorial on amortized optimization
venue: Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning
summary: Introduces the foundations of amortized optimization, which uses learning to predict solutions to repeated, similar problems. Overviews applications in variational inference, sparse coding, meta-learning, control, reinforcement learning, convex optimization, optimal transport and deep equilibrium networks.

title: Meta-Learning in Neural Networks: A Survey
summary: Describes the contemporary meta-learning landscape, defining the field and positioning it relative to transfer learning and hyperparameter optimization. Proposes a new taxonomy of methods, surveys applications such as few-shot and reinforcement learning, and discusses challenges.

title: A Survey of Deep Meta-Learning
authors: Mike Huisman, Jan N. van Rijn, Aske Plaat
summary: Surveys deep meta-learning after laying a theoretical foundation, categorizing key methods as metric-based, model-based or optimization-based techniques. Identifies open challenges such as evaluation on heterogeneous benchmarks and reducing computational cost.

title: Meta-Learning: A Survey
summary: Provides an overview of meta-learning, the practice of learning from how machine learning approaches perform across many tasks in order to learn new tasks faster. Covers its use in designing pipelines and architectures and replacing hand-engineered algorithms.

title: A Perspective View and Survey of Meta-Learning
summary: Surveys meta-learning from a classical perspective that frames the field as dynamic bias selection, and presents an early overview of the area.

title: Meta-learning approaches for few-shot learning: A survey of recent advances
summary: Surveys meta-learning approaches for few-shot learning after a brief introduction, organizing recent methods into metric-based, memory-based and learning-based families. Discusses current challenges and directions for future research.

title: Generalizing from a Few Examples: A Survey on Few-Shot Learning
summary: Surveys few-shot learning from a formal definition, distinguishing it from related problems and arguing the core issue is unreliable empirical risk. Categorizes methods by how prior knowledge is used: data, model or algorithm, and discusses pros, cons and future directions.

title: Meta-learning in natural and artificial intelligence
summary: Reviews meta-learning across biological and artificial intelligence, recasting research from cognitive science, psychology and neuroscience within a common framework. Discusses recent points of interaction between AI and neuroscience and new directions arising from this perspective.

title: Deep Learning in Neural Networks: An Overview
summary: Reviews the history of deep learning, distinguishing shallow from deep learners by the depth of their credit assignment paths. Covers supervised learning including the history of backpropagation, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, evolutionary computation, and indirect search for short programs encoding large networks.

title: Annotated History of Modern AI and Deep Learning
summary: Presents a timeline of significant events in the history of neural networks, machine learning, deep learning, AI and mathematics, crediting foundational contributors from the chain rule onward. Frames machine learning as credit assignment and supplements an earlier deep learning survey.

title: Fast weight programming and linear transformers: from machine learning to neurobiology
summary: Reviews Fast Weight Programmers, recurrent networks with matrix-form hidden states whose fast weights are programmed by a trained network, covering technical foundations, computational characteristics, links to transformers and state space models, and synaptic plasticity models in the brain.

title: Efficient Attention Mechanisms for Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Surveys efficient attention for large language models, split into linear attention (kernel approximations, recurrent formulations, fast-weight dynamics) and sparse attention (fixed patterns, block-wise routing, clustering), covering algorithms, hardware considerations, and pretrained models using efficient or hybrid local-global attention designs.

title: Combinations of genetic algorithms and neural networks: a survey of the state of the art
authors: J. David Schaffer, L. Darrell Whitley, Larry J. Eshelman
summary: Reviews early work in which genetic algorithms set neural network weights, architectures, and learning parameters, giving a state-of-the-art overview of the combination.

title: A Taxonomy for Artificial Embryogeny
summary: Organizes indirect and developmental encodings into a taxonomy with five dimensions, providing a framework for classifying and comparing approaches that grow solutions rather than specifying them directly.

title: Neuroevolution: from architectures to learning
authors: Dario Floreano, Peter Dürr, Claudio Mattiussi
summary: Reviews neuroevolution from evolving architectures to evolving learning, contrasting direct and developmental encodings and covering the evolution of plasticity rules.

title: Designing neural networks through neuroevolution
summary: Surveys neuroevolution at deep-learning scale, covering evolution strategies and genetic algorithms for weights, HyperNEAT and CPPN encodings, novelty search, and open-endedness.

title: Neuroevolution in Games: State of the Art and Open Challenges
summary: Surveys neuroevolution applied to games, analysing work along five axes: the role neuroevolution plays in a game, network types, how networks are evolved, how fitness is determined, and input types, plus open challenges.

title: Neuroevolution in Deep Neural Networks: Current Trends and Future Challenges
summary: Reviews evolutionary algorithms used for architectural configuration and training of deep neural networks, evaluating strengths and limitations, and identifying current issues, challenges, and promising future research directions.

title: Survey on Evolutionary Deep Learning: Principles, Algorithms, Applications and Open Issues
summary: Analyzes evolutionary deep learning through an AutoML lens, introducing a taxonomy of what and how to evolve across the pipeline from feature engineering and model generation to deployment, with focus on solution representation and search paradigms.

title: Lights and Shadows in Evolutionary Deep Learning: Taxonomy, Critical Methodological Analysis, Cases of Study, Learned Lessons, Recommendations and Challenges
summary: Reviews and critically examines bio-inspired optimization combined with deep learning along three axes: a taxonomy with historical perspective, a methodological critique with two case studies and recommendations, and challenges for future research.

title: A Survey on Evolutionary Neural Architecture Search
summary: Reviews over 200 papers on evolutionary computation methods for neural architecture search, organized by core components, discussing their design principles and justifications, and outlining current challenges and future research.

title: Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning: A Survey
authors: Hui Bai, Ran Cheng, Yaochu Jin
summary: Surveys methods integrating evolutionary computation into reinforcement learning, categorized by RL research field: hyperparameter optimization, policy search, exploration, reward shaping, meta-RL, and multi-objective RL, then discusses future directions in efficient methods, benchmarks, and scalable platforms.

title: Bridging Evolutionary Algorithms and Reinforcement Learning: A Comprehensive Survey on Hybrid Algorithms
summary: Surveys hybrids of evolutionary algorithms and reinforcement learning in three directions: EA-assisted optimization of RL, RL-assisted optimization of EA, and synergistic optimization, analyzing research branches in each, the problems they address, and open challenges.

title: Neuroevolution: Harnessing Creativity in AI Agent Design
summary: Presents a textbook on neuroevolution rather than a survey, including a chapter on indirect encodings spanning developmental, grammatical, and hypernetwork approaches, HyperNEAT, and self-attention viewed as a dynamic indirect encoding.

title: Evolution strategies – A comprehensive introduction
summary: Introduces evolution strategies, providing a comprehensive introductory overview of this family of evolutionary optimization algorithms and serving as a general entry point to the topic.

title: The CMA Evolution Strategy: A Tutorial
summary: Introduces CMA-ES, a stochastic method for real-parameter optimization of non-linear, non-convex functions, motivating and deriving the algorithm from intuitive concepts and from requirements of continuous-domain search.

title: Evolution strategies for continuous optimization: A survey of the state-of-the-art
summary: Reviews the state of the art in evolution strategies, a family of evolutionary algorithms for optimizing over continuous search spaces, as a survey of methods developed in this area.

title: Derivative-free optimization methods
authors: Jeffrey Larson, Matt Menickelly, Stefan M. Wild
summary: Reviews derivative-free, or zeroth-order, optimization for black-box objectives, categorizing methods by assumed properties of the function and method features: deterministic methods, randomized methods, structured objectives, stochastic oracles, and constraint handling.

title: A Primer on Zeroth-Order Optimization in Signal Processing and Machine Learning
summary: Reviews zeroth-order optimization, which uses only function evaluations through gradient estimation, descent direction computation, and solution update, covering underlying intuition, optimization principles, convergence analysis advances, and applications such as black-box robustness evaluation, explanation generation, and sensor management.

title: What is the State of Neural Network Pruning?
summary: Presents a meta-analysis of pruning literature, aggregating results across 81 papers and controlled pruning of hundreds of models, finding a lack of standardized benchmarks and metrics, and introducing ShrinkBench, an open-source evaluation framework.

title: Sparsity in Deep Learning: Pruning and growth for efficient inference and training in neural networks
summary: Surveys sparsity in deep learning and provides a tutorial on sparsification for inference and training, distilling more than 300 papers on removing and adding network elements, training strategies, and exploiting sparsity on hardware, plus open problems.

title: A Survey on Deep Neural Network Pruning-Taxonomy, Comparison, Analysis, and Recommendations
authors: Hongrong Cheng, Miao Zhang, Javen Qinfeng Shi
summary: Reviews pruning in a four-part taxonomy: universal or specific speedup, when to prune, how to prune, and fusion with other compression; compares eight pairs of contrast settings and covers LLM and multimodal model pruning.

title: Structured Pruning for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks: A survey
summary: Surveys structured pruning of deep convolutional networks, comparing techniques by filter ranking, regularization, dynamic execution, neural architecture search, the lottery ticket hypothesis, and applications, while contrasting them with unstructured pruning and outlining research opportunities.

title: A Survey of Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
summary: Examines research on the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis, the claim that dense networks contain sparse winning subnetworks, from several perspectives, discusses issues in existing work such as efficiency and scalability, and lists directions for further exploration.

title: A Survey of Model Compression and Acceleration for Deep Neural Networks
summary: Reviews techniques for compacting and accelerating DNN models in four categories: parameter pruning and quantization, low-rank factorization, transferred or compact convolutional filters, and knowledge distillation, analyzing each, with evaluation metrics, datasets, benchmark efforts, and future challenges.

title: Model Compression and Hardware Acceleration for Neural Networks: A Comprehensive Survey
summary: Surveys techniques for compressing neural networks and the hardware used to accelerate them, treating algorithmic model compression and hardware acceleration as the two main areas of coverage.

title: Pruning and Quantization for Deep Neural Network Acceleration: A Survey
summary: Surveys pruning and quantization for accelerating deep networks, separating static from dynamic pruning and comparing element-, channel-, shape-, filter-, layer- and network-wise granularities. Covers quantization to 8-bit and lower, including binary networks, and offers practical guidance.

title: A Survey of Quantization Methods for Efficient Neural Network Inference
summary: Surveys approaches to quantizing numerical values in deep neural network computations, covering the advantages and disadvantages of current methods and presenting a snapshot of this active research area for efficient inference.

title: An Overview of Neural Network Compression
summary: Reviews older and current compression techniques for deep networks, including pruning, quantization, tensor decomposition, knowledge distillation and their combinations, mostly in the context of recurrent, convolutional and self-attention architectures.

title: A Survey on Deep Neural Network Compression: Challenges, Overview, and Solutions
authors: Rahul Mishra, Hari Prabhat Gupta, Tanima Dutta
summary: Reviews DNN compression literature aimed at reducing storage and computation for resource-constrained IoT devices, dividing approaches into network pruning, sparse representation, bit precision, knowledge distillation and miscellaneous categories, with challenges per category and future directions.

title: Knowledge Distillation: A Survey
summary: Surveys knowledge distillation, in which a small student model learns from a large teacher, organized by knowledge categories, training schemes, teacher-student architectures, distillation algorithms, performance comparison and applications, plus open challenges and future directions.

title: A Survey on Model Compression and Acceleration for Pretrained Language Models
summary: Reviews compression and acceleration of Transformer-based pretrained language models, focusing on the inference stage and covering benchmarks, metrics and methodology within the broader context of efficient NLP.

title: A Survey on Model Compression for Large Language Models
summary: Surveys model compression techniques for large language models, covering quantization, pruning and knowledge distillation, along with benchmarking strategies and evaluation metrics for assessing compressed models.

title: Model Compression and Efficient Inference for Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Investigates compression and efficient inference for large language models from an algorithmic view, categorizing methods into quantization, pruning, distillation, compact architecture design and dynamic networks, distinguishing medium from large models, and introducing inference frameworks.

title: A Survey on Transformer Compression
summary: Reviews compression methods for Transformer-based language and vision models, categorized into pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation and efficient architecture design such as Mamba, RetNet and RWKV, and examines relations among the methods.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Compression Algorithms for Language Models
summary: Surveys language-model compression algorithms spanning pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation, low-rank approximation, parameter sharing and efficient architecture design, summarizing overall trends, analyzing representative algorithms in depth, and proposing future research topics.

title: A Survey of Low-bit Large Language Models: Basics, Systems, and Algorithms
summary: Surveys low-bit quantization for large language models from basic, system and algorithm perspectives: data formats and concepts, frameworks across hardware platforms, and techniques and toolkits for low-bit training and inference.

title: Efficient Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Reviews efficient large language model research through a taxonomy of three categories: model-centric, data-centric and framework-centric approaches. Links to a maintained repository that organizes the featured papers.

title: A Survey on Efficient Inference for Large Language Models
summary: Surveys efficient LLM inference, analyzing causes of inefficiency such as model size, quadratic attention and autoregressive decoding, and organizing the literature into data-level, model-level and system-level optimization, with comparative experiments on representative methods.

title: Backdoor Learning: A Survey
summary: Surveys backdoor attacks and defenses in deep learning, categorizing existing work, offering a unified framework for analyzing poisoning-based attacks, relating backdoors to adversarial attacks and data poisoning, and summarizing benchmark datasets.

title: Backdoor Attacks and Countermeasures on Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Review
summary: Organizes backdoor attacks into six categories by attacker capability and pipeline stage and defenses into four classes, comparing their strengths and weaknesses and covering beneficial uses such as intellectual property protection, honeypots and data deletion verification.

title: Dataset Security for Machine Learning: Data Poisoning, Backdoor Attacks, and Defenses
summary: Categorizes dataset vulnerabilities and exploits in machine learning, covering poisoning and backdoor threat models, defenses and open problems, and develops a unified taxonomy of the threat models and the relationships among them.

title: An Overview of Backdoor Attacks Against Deep Neural Networks and Possible Defences
authors: Wei Guo, Benedetta Tondi, Mauro Barni
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing 2022
summary: Reviews published work on training-time backdoor attacks against deep networks and their defenses, classifying them by the attacker's control over training and the defender's ability to verify training data integrity and monitor the network.

title: Attacks in Adversarial Machine Learning: A Systematic Survey from the Life-cycle Perspective
summary: Reviews adversarial machine learning attacks from a life-cycle perspective, proposing a unified mathematical framework and taxonomy covering backdoor attacks, weight attacks and adversarial attacks, and clarifying connections and differences among these paradigms.

title: A Survey of Neural Trojan Attacks and Defenses in Deep Learning
authors: Jie Wang, Ghulam Mubashar Hassan, Naveed Akhtar
summary: Reviews techniques for devising Trojan attacks on deep learning and their defenses, organizing recent literature systematically and explaining key concepts with minimal assumed background, including risks from outsourced training or data annotation.

title: A Survey of Trojan Attacks and Defenses to Deep Neural Networks
summary: Surveys Trojan attacks on deep networks and countermeasures, tracing the concept from traditional Trojans to neural network Trojans, comparing attack and defense strategies, and assessing the feasibility of such attacks in real-world scenarios.

title: Architectural Backdoors in Deep Learning: A Survey of Vulnerabilities, Detection, and Defense
authors: Victoria Childress, Josh Collyer, Jodie Knapp
summary: Consolidates research on architectural backdoors embedded in a model's computational graph, spanning compiler-level manipulations, tainted AutoML pipelines and supply-chain vulnerabilities, and assesses detection and defense strategies such as static graph inspection, dynamic fuzzing and partial formal verification.

title: Backdoor Attacks and Defenses in Computer Vision Domain: A Survey
summary: Reviews computer-vision backdoor attacks and defenses using a multi-dimensional taxonomy by injection stage, trigger type, labeling strategy, representation stage and target task, and discusses where defenses succeed or fail and gaps such as supply-chain and hardware threats.

title: Data Poisoning in Deep Learning: A Survey
summary: Reviews data poisoning attacks in deep learning, categorizing them from multiple perspectives, extending the discussion to poisoning of large language models, and outlining open challenges and research directions.

title: A Survey of Recent Backdoor Attacks and Defenses in Large Language Models
summary: Surveys backdoor attacks and defenses in large language models from a fine-tuning perspective, classifying attacks into full-parameter fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning and no fine-tuning, and discussing future directions such as attacks without fine-tuning and more covert algorithms.

title: A Survey on Backdoor Threats in Large Language Models (LLMs): Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluations
summary: Surveys backdoor threats to large language models, adapting a general machine-learning attack taxonomy to training-time white-box backdoor attacks, and covers corresponding defense methods as a guideline for future research.

title: Backdoor Attacks and Countermeasures in Natural Language Processing Models: A Comprehensive Security Review
summary: Reviews backdoor attacks and countermeasures for language models, organizing attacks into four categories by attacker capability and affected stage, and countermeasures into sample inspection and model inspection, with benchmark datasets and comparative evaluations.

title: A Survey on Backdoor Attack and Defense in Natural Language Processing
summary: Reviews backdoor attacks and defenses in natural language processing, where attackers manipulate training to inject triggers, and summarizes benchmark datasets and open issues for building systems that resist such attacks.

title: Backdoor Learning for NLP: Recent Advances, Challenges, and Future Research Directions
summary: Surveys backdoor learning for NLP, covering attack techniques, applications, defenses and mitigation methods, plus evaluation metrics, benchmark datasets, threat models and open challenges, with a continually updated companion paper list.

title: A Comprehensive Overview of Backdoor Attacks in Large Language Models within Communication Networks
summary: Surveys backdoor attacks on large language models in communication networks, proposing a taxonomy of input-triggered, prompt-triggered, instruction-triggered and demonstration-triggered attacks, and analyzes benchmark datasets and open challenges.

title: Rethinking Reasoning: A Survey on Reasoning-based Backdoors in LLMs
summary: Reviews reasoning-based backdoor attacks in LLMs, proposing a taxonomy that groups them into associative, passive and active attacks, and covers defense strategies, current challenges and future research directions.

title: Unique Security and Privacy Threats of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
summary: Surveys privacy and security threats unique to large language models across four scenarios: pre-training, fine-tuning, deployment and LLM-based agents, and analyzes potential countermeasures for each scenario.

title: Safety at Scale: A Comprehensive Survey of Large Model and Agent Safety
summary: Reviews safety research on vision foundation, language, vision-language and diffusion models and model-powered agents, with a taxonomy of threats from adversarial and backdoor attacks to jailbreaks and extraction, plus defenses, benchmarks and open challenges.

title: A Comprehensive Survey in LLM(-Agent) Full Stack Safety: Data, Training and Deployment
summary: Surveys LLM and agent safety across the full lifecycle of data preparation, pre-training, post-training, deployment and commercialization, drawing on over 800 papers to organize security issues holistically.

title: A Survey of Bit-Flip Attacks on Deep Neural Network and Corresponding Defense Methods
summary: Surveys bit-flip attacks on deep neural networks and corresponding defense methods, covering fault-injection techniques such as RowHammer, clock glitching and laser injection.

title: Security of Neural Networks from Hardware Perspective: A Survey and Beyond
authors: Qian Xu, Md Tanvir Arafin, Gang Qu
summary: Surveys hardware-level security threats to deep neural networks, including fault injection, and discusses directions beyond the surveyed work.

title: Artificial Neural Networks and Fault Injection Attacks
summary: Examines security assessment of neural network accelerators under fault injection attacks, comparing their assets with those of cryptographic systems to define threat models, and explores fault attacks mounted on such platforms.

title: Exploiting Vulnerabilities in Deep Neural Networks: Adversarial and Fault-Injection Attacks
authors: Faiq Khalid, Muhammad Abdullah Hanif, Muhammad Shafique
summary: Overviews vulnerabilities of deep neural networks in cyber-physical systems, covering adversarial and fault-injection attacks, challenges in practical implementation, and prospective approaches toward robust, resilient DNN-based systems.

title: A Survey on Impact of Transient Faults on BNN Inference Accelerators
authors: Navid Khoshavi, Connor Broyles, Yu Bi
summary: Examines the impact of soft errors on binarized neural network inference accelerators, using fault injection on image classifiers trained on CIFAR-10 and MNIST to show drastic accuracy drops.

title: A Survey on Failure Analysis and Fault Injection in AI Systems
summary: Surveys failure analysis and fault injection approaches across six layers of AI systems, analyzing 160 papers and repositories to build a taxonomy of failures and assess what faults injection tools can simulate.

title: Harmful Fine-tuning Attacks and Defenses for Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: Reviews harmful fine-tuning attacks and defenses for LLMs, formulating the threat model and organizing the literature by attack setting, defense design and evaluation methodology, with a curated companion paper list.

title: On Evaluating the Durability of Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
summary: Argues that evaluating durable safeguards for open-weight LLMs against adversarial fine-tuning is difficult, using case studies to show evaluation pitfalls and urging claims limited to well-defined, rigorously examined threat models.

title: Open Technical Problems in Open-Weight AI Model Risk Management
summary: Presents 16 open technical challenges for open-weight model safety across training data, training algorithms, evaluations, deployment and ecosystem monitoring, arguing that openness about research and evaluations is key.

title: Open Problems in Technical AI Governance
summary: Introduces technical AI governance and presents a taxonomy and incomplete catalog of its open problems, as a resource for technical researchers and funders seeking to contribute to AI governance.

title: Evolutionary Computation in the Era of Large Language Model: Survey and Roadmap
summary: Surveys the interplay of evolutionary algorithms and LLMs, categorizing work into LLM-enhanced EA and EA-enhanced LLM, with integrated methods spanning code generation, software engineering and neural architecture search, plus a roadmap.

title: When Large Language Models Meet Evolutionary Algorithms: Potential Enhancements and Challenges
summary: Reviews conceptual parallels between LLMs and evolutionary algorithms at a micro level, then analyzes interdisciplinary research at a macro level, focusing on evolutionary fine-tuning and LLM-enhanced evolutionary algorithms.

title: Exploring the Improvement of Evolutionary Computation via Large Language Models
summary: Offers a forward-looking overview of how LLMs can improve evolutionary computation, focusing on the algorithms themselves, population design and additional enhancements.

title: When Large Language Model Meets Optimization
summary: Reviews the combination of LLMs and optimization algorithms, covering how LLMs support modeling and decision-making in optimization and how optimization algorithms refine LLM architectures and output quality.

title: Deep Insights into Automated Optimization with Large Language Models and Evolutionary Algorithms
summary: Reviews LLM use in optimization, focusing on LLMs as solution generators and algorithm designers, and proposes an LLM-EA paradigm analyzed through individual representation, variation operators and fitness evaluation.

title: A Systematic Survey on Large Language Models for Algorithm Design
summary: Surveys LLMs for algorithm design with a taxonomy of LLM roles as optimizers, predictors, extractors and designers, synthesizing literature across three pipeline phases and applications, and outlining open challenges.
