title: A Systematic Survey on Large Language Models for Evolutionary Optimization: From Modeling to Solving
summary: Reviews large language models for evolutionary optimization through a workflow of optimization modeling and optimization solving, splitting solving into stand-alone optimizers, embedded low-level components, and high-level managers for algorithm selection and generation, plus benchmarks and applications.

title: Large Language Models and Evolutionary Computation: A Critical Review of Bidirectional Interaction, Automated Algorithm Design, and Co-Adaptive Systems
summary: Reviews the bidirectional interaction between LLMs and evolutionary computation, covering EC improving LLM systems via prompt optimization and architecture search, LLMs improving EC via metaheuristic and heuristic design, and co-adaptive feedback-loop frameworks.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search
summary: Surveys LLM-guided evolutionary search, exemplified by AlphaEvolve, and presents itself as the first survey dedicated to this research direction.

title: Large Language Models as Optimizers: A Survey of Direct vs. Tool-Augmented Approaches and Their Performance Frontiers
summary: Surveys LLMs used as optimizers across three paradigms: direct optimization via iterative prompting, tool-augmented optimization that orchestrates external solvers, and tool-creating optimization that discovers reusable algorithms. Describes benchmark-based performance frontiers and argues for trade-offs between direct and tool-augmented approaches.

title: AutoML in the Age of Large Language Models: Current Challenges, Future Opportunities and Risks
summary: Explores the symbiosis of AutoML and LLMs, surveying existing work on enhancing AutoML with LLMs and on using AutoML to improve LLMs, and critically assessing the risks of integrating the two fields.

title: Large Language Models for Constructing and Optimizing Machine Learning Workflows: A Survey
summary: Reviews how LLMs construct and optimize machine learning workflows, organized around data and feature engineering, model selection and hyperparameter optimization, and workflow evaluation, with discussion of advantages, limitations, open challenges and future directions.

title: Large Language Model-based Data Science Agent: A Survey
summary: Reviews LLM-based agents for data science from two perspectives: agent design principles covering roles, execution, knowledge and reflection, and data science processes such as preprocessing, model development, evaluation and visualization, linked by a dual-perspective framework.

title: A Survey on Self-Evolution of Large Language Models
summary: Surveys self-evolution of LLMs as iterative cycles of experience acquisition, experience refinement, updating and evaluation, categorizes evolution objectives for LLMs and LLM-based agents, and gives a taxonomy and insights for each module.

title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence
summary: Reviews self-evolving agents along three dimensions: what to evolve across agent components such as models, memory, tools and architecture, when to adapt by stage, and how, plus benchmarks, applications in coding, education and healthcare, and open challenges.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents: A New Paradigm Bridging Foundation Models and Lifelong Agentic Systems
summary: Reviews self-evolving AI agents through a unified feedback-loop framework of system inputs, agent system, environment and optimisers, surveying techniques targeting each component, domain-specific strategies in biomedicine, programming and finance, and evaluation, safety and ethics.

title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
summary: Frames modern self-improving agents as a foundation model coupled with a scaffold of prompts, memory, tools and control logic, formalizes self-improvement as a self-induced update operator, and organizes prior work by update target and driving signal.

title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
authors: Mingguang Chen, Licheng Wang, Bo Qu
summary: Surveys 1,250 arXiv papers from 2024–2026 along two axes: what the system improves and the degree of loop closure, separating bounded self-refinement from open-ended recursive self-improvement and ordering evaluator signals into a verification hierarchy.

title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: A Survey
summary: Surveys recursive self-improvement in AI, contrasting approaches that automate the design of AI infrastructure with those that repair existing systems.

title: AI4AI Survey: From Long-Horizon Agents to Recursive Self-Improvement—Definitions, Reliable Horizons, and Open Problems
summary: Surveys the progression from long-horizon agents to recursive self-improvement, covering definitions, reliable horizons and open problems, with a section on self-modifying systems and a thesis about a composition gap.

title: Position: Agentic Evolution is the Path to Evolving LLMs
summary: Argues that agentic evolution, in which an autonomous evolver agent drives deployment-time adaptation, is the future of LLM adaptation, introduces the A-Evolve framework, and proposes an evolution-scaling hypothesis tying adaptation capacity to evolution compute.

title: AI-GAs: AI-generating algorithms, an alternate paradigm for producing general artificial intelligence
summary: Argues that the AI-generating algorithm approach, built on three pillars of meta-learning architectures, meta-learning learning algorithms and generating learning environments, deserves more research investment than the manual approach to general AI, and discusses safety and ethics.

title: Open-Endedness is Essential for Artificial Superhuman Intelligence
summary: Argues that open-endedness, formally defined through novelty and learnability, is essential for artificial superhuman intelligence, outlines a path via open-ended systems built on foundation models, and examines safety implications.

title: Safety in Self-Evolving LLM Agent Systems: Threats, Amplification, and Case Studies
summary: Analyzes security and privacy threats in self-evolving LLM agent systems using a matrix of five functional modules by five lifecycle stages, identifying seven amplification effects and comparing two open-source frameworks in case studies.

title: A Survey of AI Scientists
authors: Guiyao Tie, Pan Zhou, Lichao Sun
summary: Surveys AI scientist systems through a six-stage framework spanning literature review, idea generation, experimental preparation, experimental execution, scientific writing and paper generation, and traces the field's evolution from foundational modules to closed-loop systems and current scalability work.

title: From Automation to Autonomy: A Survey on Large Language Models in Scientific Discovery
summary: Surveys LLMs in scientific discovery through a three-level taxonomy of Tool, Analyst and Scientist that reflects escalating autonomy across the research lifecycle, and identifies challenges including robotic automation, self-improvement and ethical governance.

title: Towards Scientific Intelligence: A Survey of LLM-based Scientific Agents
summary: Reviews LLM-based scientific agents, covering their architectures, design, benchmarks, applications and ethical considerations, and how they differ from general-purpose agents in tasks from hypothesis generation to experiment design, data analysis and simulation.

title: From AI for Science to Agentic Science: A Survey on Autonomous Scientific Discovery
summary: Reviews autonomous scientific discovery across life sciences, chemistry, materials science and physics, unifying process-, autonomy- and mechanism-oriented perspectives in a framework with five core capabilities and a four-stage discovery workflow.

title: AI4Research: A Survey of Artificial Intelligence for Scientific Research
summary: Surveys AI for scientific research with a systematic taxonomy of five mainstream tasks, identifies research gaps and future directions on rigor, scalability and societal impact, and compiles applications, data corpora and tools.

title: LLM4SR: A Survey on Large Language Models for Scientific Research
summary: Surveys the roles of LLMs across four stages of the research cycle: hypothesis discovery, experiment planning and implementation, scientific writing and peer reviewing, covering task-specific methods, evaluation benchmarks, challenges and future directions.

title: Agentic AI for Scientific Discovery: A Survey of Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions
summary: Surveys agentic AI for scientific discovery, categorizing existing systems and tools and their progress in chemistry, biology and materials science, and covering evaluation metrics, implementation frameworks, datasets, challenges such as reliability and ethics, and human-AI collaboration directions.

title: Algorithms for Verifying Deep Neural Networks
summary: Surveys methods for soundly verifying input-output properties of deep neural networks, drawing on reachability analysis, optimization, and search. Discusses connections between algorithms and provides pedagogical implementations compared on benchmark problems.

title: A Survey of Safety and Trustworthiness of Deep Neural Networks: Verification, Testing, Adversarial Attack and Defence, and Interpretability
summary: Reviews research on making deep neural networks safe and trustworthy, organized around four aspects: verification, testing, adversarial attack and defence, and interpretability. Covers 202 papers, most published after 2017.

title: SoK: Certified Robustness for Deep Neural Networks
authors: Linyi Li, Tao Xie, Bo Li
summary: Systematizes certifiably robust approaches for deep neural networks, providing a taxonomy of robustness verification and robust training methods and discussing their strengths, limitations, and connections. Includes an open-source unified platform evaluating more than 20 representative approaches.

title: Introduction to Neural Network Verification
venue: Foundations and Trends in Programming Languages 2021
summary: Introduces foundational ideas from formal verification and their adaptation to reasoning about the safety, security, correctness, and robustness of neural networks and deep learning, in book-length form.

title: Adversarial Robustness of Deep Neural Networks: A Survey from a Formal Verification Perspective
summary: Surveys 39 works on adversarial robustness verification for neural networks, analyzing how robustness is formulated and which verification techniques are used. Classifies techniques by property specification, problem reduction, and reasoning strategies.

title: A Review of Formal Methods applied to Machine Learning
summary: Reviews formal methods for verifying machine learning systems, first recalling established methods in avionic software. Notes most methods target trained neural networks using SMT, optimization, or abstract interpretation, and also covers support vector machines and decision tree ensembles.

title: First Three Years of the International Verification of Neural Networks Competition (VNN-COMP)
summary: Summarizes and meta-analyzes the first three annual neural network verification competitions, held in 2020, 2021, and 2022, covering processes, rules, results, and observed trends across problem classes such as image classification, neural control, and reinforcement learning.

title: Towards Verified Artificial Intelligence
authors: Sanjit A. Seshia, Dorsa Sadigh, S. Shankar Sastry
summary: Considers verified AI, meaning systems with provable correctness assurances, from a formal methods perspective. Describes five challenges for achieving it and five corresponding principles for addressing them.

title: Neural Network Verification is a Programming Language Challenge
summary: Argues that neural network verification challenges should be formulated as programming language challenges, and suggests possible future solutions drawing on insights from the programming language community.

title: Model checking deep neural networks: opportunities and challenges
summary: Takes a model-checking perspective on deep neural networks, outlining the opportunities and challenges of applying that approach to them.

title: Transfer Learning for Reinforcement Learning Domains: A Survey
summary: Surveys the literature on transfer learning in classical reinforcement learning domains, giving an overview of how the topic has been studied.

title: Transfer Learning in Deep Reinforcement Learning: A Survey
summary: Surveys transfer learning approaches in deep reinforcement learning, proposing a framework that categorizes them and analyzes their goals, methodologies, compatible reinforcement learning backbones, and practical applications. Also connects transfer learning to related topics and outlines future challenges.

title: Towards Continual Reinforcement Learning: A Review and Perspectives
summary: Reviews formulations and approaches to continual reinforcement learning, offering taxonomies of formulations, based on scope and driver of non-stationarity, and of methods. Covers evaluation benchmarks and metrics, and open problems linking the field to neuroscience.

title: A Survey of Zero-shot Generalisation in Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Surveys zero-shot generalisation in deep reinforcement learning, using a unifying formalism to categorise existing benchmarks and methods. Offers a critical discussion with recommendations, including building benchmarks in underexplored settings such as offline RL and reward-function variation.

title: Combining Trained Models in Reinforcement Learning
summary: Presents a PRISMA-guided systematic review of pretrained knowledge reuse in deep reinforcement learning, narrowing 589 retrieved records to 15 empirical studies. Analyzes them by source-target similarity, diversity of reused models, and fairness of comparisons against from-scratch baselines.

title: devichand579/gepa_wsp
summary: Reflective GEPA loop in which LLMs (DeepSeek, MiniMax, Nemotron) propose weight edits for MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, SST-2 and diffusion networks, with no parameter-gradient updates. 45 retained trajectories, 3 seeds, 60 mutations, compared to Adam. It improves one-shot statistical weight programs but does not generally replace Adam.

title: Flecart/weight-programming
summary: Replication and stress tests of 'Sparks of Weight Space Programming'. Hand-written MinAtar networks match published scores; the Kinetix car fix succeeds in 1,024/1,024 episodes. A Breakout network scores 517 versus 534 for a Python script with the same algorithm. Tests obfuscation (156/156 correct) and Claude Opus 5.5 writing networks.

title: Does Claude have it too? Replicating 'Sparks of Weight-Space Programming'
summary: Replication of the MinAtar write-from-scratch experiment with Claude Opus 5.5, using the same prompts and scorer. In each game one of three one-shot replies reached 87%, 97% and 86% of GPT-6 Astra's score; median replies reached 51%, 14% and 62%. Claude beats PPO at 100M steps in every game.

title: Weights or Skills? A Survey of Robot-Learning Techniques: from Action-Predicting Weights to Robots that Write their Own Skills
summary: Organizes robot learning by whether competence lives in frozen policy weights (VLA models) or in executable skills that agents write and refine as code. It ranks code-as-policy methods by degree of self-improvement across 77 systems and notes that only the code sense of skill improves without gradient updates.

title: Where Does Knowledge Live? Representational, Causal, and Editable Localization in Language Models: A Survey
summary: Separates three senses of knowledge localization in language models (representational, causal and editable) and reviews the evidence that they disagree: causal tracing can miss the best edit site and superposition makes single neurons polysemantic.

title: A Survey on Actionable Interpretability in Large Language Models
authors: Jie Cai, Mafizur Rahman, James Enouen, Lijun Qian, Yan Liu
summary: Reviews attributional and mechanistic interpretability methods by whether they lead to an intervention, and how they support hallucination mitigation, knowledge editing, fairness, safety and efficiency in LLMs and VLMs.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of LLM Behavior: A Survey
authors: Priya Pitre, Jun Hou, Ziyu Yao, Naren Ramakrishnan, Xuan Wang
summary: Surveys 229 papers across five behavior families (epistemic, linguistic, reasoning, safety, social) and grades mechanistic evidence on five levels, from decodability to generalization.

title: Knowledge Mechanisms Across the Lifecycle of Large Language Models
summary: Traces how knowledge is acquired, represented, used, revised and transferred inside LLMs with a stage-driven taxonomy, moving from the model-as-knowledge-base view to micro-level mechanisms such as localization, superposition and knowledge conflict.

title: Weight-Space Programming on Qwen3-ASR-0.6B: Nine Independent Agent Edits, Random-Direction Controls, and a Missing Attention Mask
summary: Applied the Sparks repair protocol to speech recognition. Nine Claude agent edits each reduced a silence-induced language-tagging failure, and the real edit beat matched random-direction controls in 26 of 27 comparisons. The failure turned out to be largely a missing attention mask in the inference backend, which the edits compensated for in weight space.

title: The Mathematics of Weight-Space Programming
summary: Gives conditions under which a selective edit to a transformer's final feed-forward module is possible, minimum-cost edits under explicit preservation constraints, and certificates of infeasibility. The editors are explicit algorithms, not LLMs; on GPT-2 CounterFact edits, interval constraints improved neighbor retention by about 20 points.

title: Rohitthimaya/weight-space-programming
summary: Edits Stable Diffusion 1.5 weights directly, with no training, so cat prompts produce dogs. Round 1 copies 3 token-embedding rows (2,304 weights, 0.00022%). Round 2 edits only the UNet, applying a rank-3 map to 32 cross-attention to_k/to_v matrices (1.79%). CLIP labels 15 of 15 cat images as dog, with 3 control prompts unchanged.

title: Can a language model repair a network's weights by reading them?
summary: Code, frozen decision rules and run records for an extended abstract on language-model weight repair. In an unconstrained pilot, two editor models reached the task ceiling by writing a replacement network. Under a bounded numeric-edit budget, neither repaired the trained network beyond the threshold, while projected gradient descent did on every seed. One task, one architecture, five seeds.

title: Weight-Space Programming: an independent reproduction
summary: Reruns two experiments from the original report with the same prompts and gpt-6-astra, tools off. Breakout: a fresh answer scores 416.8 ± 6.9 over 1,000 games (original weights re-scored 502.9 ± 7.7). Car: 1 of 4 independent answers works, 0 to 1,024 of 1,024 test games.

title: Weight-space programming on a character recognizer
summary: Claude as a coding agent repairs a planted defect (50% of E relabeled V) in a 108,271-parameter EMNIST CNN by rewriting 35 weights, no gradients: E accuracy 75.2% to 97.0% (seed 0). Reports five seeds, weights-only and data-assisted tiers, and a fine-tuning control.

title: wsp: weight space programming
summary: Harnesses, agent prompts and results for LLM agents that explain, write or graft network weights without training. Experiments: Pong policy, 8.6k-parameter help-desk transformer (97% exact replies on test set), tool-calling chatbot, GenGPT assistant (79–81% hidden test, 0 safety violations); a general-chat attempt was a negative result.

title: Banking77 by weight-space programming
summary: Claude Opus 5.5, with numpy and 30 forward passes, writes a 77-way intent classifier into 188 layer-31 neurons of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct (0.029% of weights), no gradients. Banking77 test accuracy 91.95%, versus 91.1% for a fine-tuned reference and 58.7% zero-shot; retention 40/40.

title: The Astra weight edit on Qwen3.5-0.8B: a GSM8K rerun with transformers and a 16K budget
summary: Reruns the Astra edit of Qwen3.5-0.8B (130,188 weights) on 100 GSM8K problems with transformers and a 16,384-token limit. Thinking on: 7 to 50 correct; thinking off: 47 to 43. Verdict rule written before generation; independent recheck included.

title: Weight-Space Programming and Gradient Optimization on Nonconvex Algorithmic Tasks
summary: A language model writes weights for fixed small networks on ten algorithmic tasks (29 task-architecture pairs, three starts, 87 settings), compared with gradient-based optimizer pipelines. Examples-only WSP matches every binary64 extrapolation reference in 30 of 87 settings; gradient descent and gradient descent plus L-BFGS match in zero. Iterative WSP examples-only RMSE total drops from about 1.06 trillion to 2.03 billion.

title: Weight-space programming with Claude Opus 5.5
summary: Independent replication of Sparks of Weight-Space Programming with Claude Opus 5.5 instead of GPT-6 Astra, on Gymnasium, ALE and PettingZoo environments. Probes: reading Atari policies (3/4 games read), fixing failing policies (MountainCar 0% to 100%, LunarLander 0% to 85.6%), writing policies zero-shot, writing a 9x9 Go network, and identifying a sycophantic Gemma 3 270M finetune (6/6).

title: Independently Discovered Weight Edits Compose: A Replication and Extension of Weight-Space Programming
summary: Replication of Sparks of Weight-Space Programming on Qwen3.5-0.8B: Astra's edit scores 46.8% on MATH-500 against a 6% base. Claude Opus 5.5 writes a second edit; stacking both reaches 52.2% on all 500 problems, with 31% fewer tokens than Astra's edit. A random edit of the same size reaches 20% on the first 100 problems.

title: Weight-space programming on a regulatory-genomics CNN: public release 1
summary: Preregistered, blinded test of whether Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code can detect and remove a planted shortcut in a CTCF-binding CNN from its weights, without gradients. 56 sessions on 18 planted and 10 clean models. Detection: D = 0.396 [0.021, 0.792], one-sided p = 0.0177. Repair: 2 of 36 planted-model sessions met the fix criterion.

title: Weight-space programming, but for SQL
summary: Independent test of the MIT report on Qwen3.5-0.8B for text-to-SQL, with Claude Fable 5.1 as editor. A 4,083-entry edit cuts the loop rate from 90.7% to 26.0% and raises accuracy from 0.7% to 6.0% on 150 BIRD Mini-Dev questions. Random edits of the same size do nothing; base with thinking off scores 7.3%.

title: Gradient-Free Weight Editing Reduces Overthinking in Qwen3.8-27B
summary: Norm-matched controlled replication of weight-space programming. A nine-layer gradient-free edit to Qwen3.8-27B cuts thinking tokens by up to 54% while accuracy rises. An equal-norm random edit on the same layers does nothing. Statistics are generated from released artifacts; bootstrap seed check flags the IFBench control interval as borderline.

title: wsp: LLM as an optimiser - weight space programming
summary: Autoresearch-style harness where an agent reads and edits network weights with a metered budget of forward passes and no optimiser. Tasks are pluggable. Reported: IFEval on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct held-out 0.351 to 0.406; one network written from zero weights for chess and 9x9 Go, held-out win rate 0.244 to 0.980.

title: WSP4Rec: Exploring weight-space programming for recommender systems
summary: Controlled study of Astra editing MovieLens-100K factorization-machine recommenders, with three training seeds, eight editor conditions, and calibration, random and title-smoothing controls. Mean test NDCG@10 base / no-title WSP / WSP+titles: 0.05801 / 0.07328 / 0.07534 (MSE), 0.10441 / 0.10490 / 0.10566 (BPR). EASE: 0.12031.

title: Weight-Space Programming Replication
summary: Replicates all eight experiments of Sparks of Weight-Space Programming with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1, using a rebuilt harness checked against Astra's released results. Experiment 1: Opus 4/4, Fable 3/4. Breakout mean score 483.6 (Opus), 38.4 (Fable), 517.4 (Astra).

title: weight-space-programming: editing SmolLM2-360M for BFCL tool calls
summary: Claude Opus 5.5 makes three weight edits to SmolLM2-360M-Instruct using 100 metered practice forwards on BFCL v4 simple_python. Practice accuracy goes from 41% to 62%; sealed 100-item holdout from 33% to 50%. Gains are from call formatting, not new knowledge.

title: Weight-space programming: local replication kit
summary: Replication kit on one 8 GB GPU. Opus 5.5 gets 4/4 and 3/3 on experiments 1-2. New experiments: writing company facts, held-out 86% against LoRA 53% (0.8B) and 96.7% against QLoRA 47% (9B, 4-bit); LiveCodeBench on 4B, thinking-off edit 52.6% to 59.5% (p about 0.05).

title: Weight-Space Programming of Variational Quantum Circuits: Large Language Models Write Quantum Circuit Parameters Without an Optimizer
authors: Debarshi Kundu, Swaroop Ghosh, Vasant Honavar
summary: GPT-6 Astra writes the angles of parameterized quantum circuits directly, with no optimizer or feedback, for VQE, QAOA and quantum machine learning. VQE is within 0.007 of the optimizer on the normalized energy scale on all 11 problem–ansatz pairs. QAOA depth-1 angles are optimal on all six graphs. A warm-started optimizer reaches its best value after a median of 1 evaluation.

title: aner-lang/aner-weight-space-programming
summary: Replays the stored weight changes of MIT's Qwen3.5-0.8B repair through Aner. Both edited BF16 tensor hashes match the manifest, 130,188 entries changed, and rollback restores the original checkpoint hash. Local inference pilots showed no accuracy gain: base 1/8 correct and edited 1/8 on eight prompts with a 2,048-token cap.

title: ZeroTang05/WSP-toolkit
summary: Toolkit to read, edit and evaluate open-weight language model weights: safetensors WeightStore, activation patching, a ProgrammingSession workspace for a model as programmer, TIES merging and SparseGPT reconstruction. On the 1,319-question GSM8K test set, Qwen3-0.6B went from 485 correct (36.77%) to 600 (45.49%) after a scaled TIES merge of three trained updates.

title: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection
authors: Chris von Csefalvay, Pranav Doma, Achyuthan Unni Krishnan, Tamás Földi
summary: Benchmark of a large editor model modifying the weights of a smaller target model (typically Gemma 3 4B IT) for ten text-editing objectives. Editors get four weight read/write tools and a fixed rollout budget. A validator applies each patch and compares it with the unmodified target. A few models lead far ahead; structured response was never solved.

title: ray-invnt/weight-space-programming-at-scale
summary: Code and logs for a blog post in which an agent (Claude Fable 5.1) edits weights without training: a MedGemma 4B skill into Gemma 3 4B, TranslateGemma 4B, Gemma 4 26B, Qwen3 4B LoRA merges and gpt-oss-120b. Includes prompts, step logs, edits, build scripts and per-question scores.

title: yahya010/wsp-ptq
summary: Agent prompt and harness for repairing a 3-bit quantized LLM by editing codes and scales, with no fitting or training. On Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B, editing 0.0008% of weights of a poorly calibrated checkpoint raised GSM8K from 71.4 to 91.6 and MATH-500 from 60.8 to 82.2.

title: manaskarra/magenta-wsp
summary: Weight-space programming experiment on Google Magenta RealTime 2. One 768×1,024 adapter matrix (0.032% of the checkpoint) is replaced by a calculated update, without backpropagation, so piano-conditioned music comes out as flute. Two blind comparisons against prompting for flute split 1–1; one listener.

title: fus3r/wspserve
summary: Forward-pass server for weight-space programming sessions, plus measurements of the released Sparks of WSP Experiment 8 logs. All 88 edits are channel scalings or rank-one projections. A single session keeps a dedicated GPU 51 to 78% busy. The server applies each edit as a per-row delta in one resident model.

title: Egzakta-AILab/wsp-lab
summary: Harness, measurements and transcripts for an editor agent editing Qwen3.8-27B in a sandboxed CPU kernel with a metered forward-pass budget and a sealed held-out test. One edited tensor targets Serbian defects: Croatian/ijekavian forms fell from 4.4% to 2–3%. GPQA Diamond was 89.0 versus 88.3.

title: khordoo/dusty-wsp
summary: GPT-6 Astra makes analytical low-rank weight edits to an 8M-parameter language model without training. A Dusty-to-Milo rename raised identity-suite success from 13/30 to 21/30 greedy. A fear-to-curiosity association edit scored 0/48 on held-out responses, matching the original.

title: Can a Language Model Write the Weights? An Empirical Study of LLM-Written Scoring Networks for Column Generation and MILP Branching, with a Bus-Driver Scheduling Application
summary: An LLM wrote small MLPs, with no gradient training, to score arcs and branching variables in column generation and SCIP branch-and-bound. On a MARTA crew-scheduling model, the written rules took 0.63x the default's time on 32 held-out instances, but SCIP's pseudocost rule did as well (ratio 0.99). On 39 MIPLIB 2017 instances it solved 19 versus 24.

title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
authors: Junru Hu, Cheng Tang, Wei Li, Hongze Zhu, et al.
summary: Studies WSP through 16 editing trajectories across seven benchmarks on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-9B. Held-out accuracy rises by up to 29.45 points on MATH-500, and modifying 1,023 parameters gives the 29.45-point gain. A Math-edited checkpoint improves GPQA Diamond, IFEval and SciBench. Six of 16 trajectories keep the original weights.

title: Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?
authors: Jusheng Zhang, Keze Wang, Liang Lin
summary: GPT-6 Astra reads π0.5 weights and edits 65 token-embedding rows with simulator feedback and no gradient updates. Success on 765 held-out paraphrases rises from 86.3% to 92.0% (exact paired p=1.31e-10). Matched random-direction edits do not help. Across 13 further robot sessions the editor declines 12 candidates.

title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming Across a Difficulty-Graded Ladder of Two-Player Games
summary: An LLM set every weight of feed-forward networks by hand, with no training data, across a four-rung game ladder (Nim, tic-tac-toe, Connect Four, a chess endgame). Ten networks were built and verified, and six have complete correctness proofs. The chess-endgame network reaches 84.1-100% on one-ply tactics but 0.57-9.13% in full adversarial play.

title: Ahmedn1/wsplab
summary: Python library that runs weight-space programming sessions: an LLM editor gets a sandboxed kernel and a forward-pass budget, edits are scored on hidden evaluation with paired statistics and a same-size random-edit control, and saved as patches that rebuild the edited model from the public base. Works on language models and other PyTorch networks.

title: DanieleMenchetti/weight-space-programming-example
summary: CPU-only notebook where Claude Opus 5.5, run through Claude Code, reads, repairs and writes the weights of tiny PyTorch MLPs without gradients. Repair changed 1 of 33 weights, taking accuracy from 66.4% to 99.8%. Writing an XOR net from scratch reached 100%. Adam baselines are included.

title: nathanrs/weight-space-lp
summary: Follow-up to the Qwen3.5-0.8B looping fix. Given the agent's loop direction, one linear-program solve chooses which down_proj neurons to change and by how much. It matches the agent's edit with 8× fewer weights. A variant that takes the direction from detected loops, with no LLM, gets about 93% of the way. A same-size steering vector scores 50.8 on MATH-500.

title: AryaGPT2022/weight-space-programming
summary: Applies weight-space programming to the BERT cross-encoder ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 used as a RAG reranker. Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code reads the weights and runs the network for at most 25 forward passes. It writes edits such as pruning, layer drop and direction projection, with no gradients. Evaluated on MS MARCO and BEIR with an audit script and data-free baselines.
